spawning.answer: The Agent is associated with Education coding features rather than normal Survival mob spawning.

interactions.answer: Supported coding tools give the Agent instructions. Ordinary animal feeding and breeding do not control it.

availability.answer: The Agent belongs to Education-related coding features. It is not an ordinary Survival mob with a natural biome or taming recipe.

identity.answer: An Agent is a programmable helper from compatible Minecraft Education features. Use compatible coding tools to direct it through building, moving, or other supported actions; it is not an ordinary Survival pet.

behavior.answer: An Agent is a programmable helper from compatible Minecraft Education features. Use compatible coding tools to direct it through building, moving, or other supported actions; it is not an ordinary Survival pet.

spawning.answer: Look in cages at pillager outposts and jail cells in woodland mansions. The original allays generate with those structures; not every cage or cell contains them.

drops.answer: An allay drops the item it was holding when it dies, but has no other normal item or experience drops.

breeding.answer: Allays duplicate rather than breed as a pair. Play a music disc in a nearby jukebox, then give a dancing allay an amethyst shard. Both allays then have a five-minute duplication cooldown; there is no baby allay.

taming.answer: Allays are not tamed like wolves. Give one an item to have it follow you and collect matching dropped items; take that item back to release it.

interactions.answer: An allay collects dropped copies of the item it holds. It can deliver to you or to a note block it recently heard. It does not mine blocks or take items out of containers.

music.answer: A note block redirects item deliveries for 30 seconds and repeated notes refresh that focus. A jukebox has a different job: a dancing allay given an amethyst shard duplicates, with a five-minute cooldown for both allays.

storage.answer: An allay collects dropped copies of the item it holds. It does not mine blocks, create new items or take items out of chests. A recently heard note block can act as a delivery point.

sunlight.answer: Sunlight alone does not make it burn like an exposed zombie or skeleton. Other hazards, such as being out of water or changing dimensions, can still matter for the species.

fire.answer: Without protection, ordinary fire and lava can damage it. Being undead, large, or adapted to a particular biome does not by itself grant fire immunity.

variants.answer: Allays duplicate into another full-sized allay rather than producing a baby. The new allay does not inherit the original custom name.

spawn_conditions.answer: Allays do not refill a cleared structure through ordinary natural spawning. Search another eligible structure or duplicate an existing allay with an amethyst shard while it dances to a jukebox.

leashing.answer: Yes. Use a lead on it to move it, then use a fence to tie it there. You can remove the lead with shears. Leashing does not tame the creature or give it immunity to hazards.

delivery.answer: Give an allay one example item. It collects matching dropped items; it does not mine blocks, duplicate your items or take them from chests. A note block heard within 16 blocks can redirect deliveries for 30 seconds. Replaying that same note block refreshes its attention; wool can block the vibration.

item_holding.answer: Use an empty hand on the allay to take back its example item. Giving it an item asks it to collect matching drops, not to duplicate the item or open chests.

experience.answer: It gives no experience when killed. Item drops and rewards from other interactions are separate.

equipment_drops.answer: An allay drops the item it was holding. This returns a carried item; it does not duplicate the item or drop an entire invented inventory.

diet.answer: Giving an allay an item tells it which dropped items to collect; handing it a food item is not the same interaction as feeding a breeding animal. To duplicate an allay, give it an amethyst shard while it dances to a nearby jukebox.

growth.answer: Allays have no baby form. Duplication makes another allay directly, so there is no baby allay to feed or wait to grow.

lifetime.answer: Allays normally have persistence in Bedrock and do not disappear through ordinary distance despawning. They can still be killed or removed by other game rules.

relocation.answer: You can use a lead to move a allay. Guide it along a safe route, keep it close enough that the lead does not break, and protect it from falls and unsuitable water or heat.

attack_style.answer: An allay does not fight players or act as a combat pet. Its job is collecting matching dropped items.

provocation.answer: Hitting an allay does not make it retaliate like a wolf. Giving it an item changes collection behavior, not an attack mode.

counterplay.answer: You do not need to fight an allay to stop it following you; take its held item back with an empty hand. Protect it from nearby hostile mobs and environmental damage.

identity.answer: An allay is a friendly flying helper mob. Give it an item and it looks for dropped matching items to bring back. It does not mine blocks or create items for you.

behavior.answer: An allay is a friendly flying helper mob. Give it an item and it looks for dropped matching items to bring back. It does not mine blocks or create items for you.

combat.answer: It does not normally attack players. Give it an item and it looks for dropped matching items to bring back. It does not mine blocks or create items for you.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 20 health points (10 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

diet_cases.answer: An allay can hold that item and collect matching dropped items. Giving it food is an item-collection instruction, not animal breeding. Duplication uses an amethyst shard while it dances to jukebox music.

spawning.answer: Lingering potions and certain special attacks create temporary effect clouds.

interactions.answer: An area-effect cloud applies its configured effect to eligible nearby entities and disappears over time. Stay out of harmful clouds; their effects depend on their source.

projectile_effects.answer: A lingering cloud affects eligible entities inside its area and shrinks as it expires or applies effects. It is a temporary area hazard, not the original potion bottle.

retrieval.answer: You cannot collect an ordinary lingering potion cloud back into its original bottle. Dragon’s breath collection is a different special cloud interaction.

identity.answer: An area-effect cloud is an invisible or particle-marked area that applies configured effects. It is used by mechanics such as lingering potions and dragon breath. Entering it can apply the corresponding effect.

behavior.answer: An area-effect cloud is an invisible or particle-marked area that applies configured effects. It is used by mechanics such as lingering potions and dragon breath. Entering it can apply the corresponding effect.

spawning.answer: Look in savanna, savanna plateau, windswept savanna, badlands, wooded badlands and eroded badlands.

drops.answer: Killing an armadillo does not provide armadillo scutes. Living armadillos shed scutes periodically, and brushing one gives a scute. Adults can give experience when killed; babies give neither items nor experience.

breeding.answer: Feed spider eyes to two nearby adult armadillos. If an armadillo rolls up before reaching its mate, it needs to be fed again.

taming.answer: Armadillos cannot be tamed. You can breed them with spider eyes and move them with a lead.

interactions.answer: Use a brush to collect scutes without killing it. Sprinting players, mounted players, damage and nearby undead can make it roll up; spiders and cave spiders avoid armadillos.

fire.answer: Without protection, it can take fire and lava damage and die. Living in a warm biome or having a particular coat color does not grant fire immunity.

sunlight.answer: Ordinary sunlight does not make this creature spontaneously burn. Fire, lava and lightning are separate hazards.

brushing.answer: Brush an armadillo to obtain an armadillo scute while keeping it alive. Adults also shed scutes periodically; killing it is not the scute-harvesting method.

land.answer: It can live on land. Still provide suitable safe terrain and protect it from fire, falls or other species-specific hazards.

age_lock.answer: Use a golden dandelion on an eligible baby to pause its aging. Use another golden dandelion on that same baby to resume aging. This is separate from feeding normal food to speed growth.

variants.answer: Armadillos have baby and adult stages. Rolling into a ball is a defensive state, not a separate breed.

spawn_conditions.answer: Bedrock armadillos need light level 7 or more in their eligible savanna or badlands habitats. A warm climate alone does not make every desert a valid armadillo biome.

leashing.answer: Yes. Use a lead on it to move it, then use a fence to tie it there. You can remove the lead with shears. Leashing does not tame the creature or give it immunity to hazards.

defense.answer: An unrolled armadillo repels spiders and cave spiders within six blocks. A rolled-up armadillo does not provide that repelling behavior; it is protecting itself rather than fighting for you.

rolling.answer: Armadillos roll up when hurt or threatened by nearby undead mobs or sprinting or mounted players. While rolled up they do not eat or follow food. Remove the threat and give it time to unroll; water, fire or attaching a lead also ends the rolled state.

experience.answer: An adult can drop 1–3 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Babies do not give death experience. These are experience points, not player levels.

experience_baby.answer: The baby does not give experience when killed. Growing into an adult changes its death reward; it is separate from experience earned by successful breeding.

experience_breeding.answer: Successful breeding gives 1–7 experience points. That reward comes from breeding, not from killing the baby. The animal’s own breeding requirements still apply.

breeding_age.answer: No. A baby cannot breed; it must grow into an adult first. Food that helps it grow is not the same as breeding food being used on an adult.

growth.answer: A baby armadillo normally takes about 20 minutes of active game time to become an adult. You can speed this up by feeding it spider eyes while it is unrolled.

diet.answer: Use spider eyes to breed adult armadillos or help babies grow. An armadillo must be unrolled to accept this feeding interaction; feeding is different from brushing it for scutes.

lifetime.answer: A naturally spawned armadillo can disappear through ordinary distance despawning unless it has become persistent. In Bedrock, a name tag is one way to prevent ordinary distance despawning; distance rules depend on simulation settings and mob state. Suitable player interactions, such as breeding, tempting with accepted food or leashing where supported, can also give persistence. A boat or minecart alone is not a blanket persistence guarantee, and persistence does not prevent death.

relocation.answer: You can use a lead to move a armadillo. Guide it along a safe route, keep it close enough that the lead does not break, and protect it from falls and unsuitable water or heat.

attack_style.answer: An armadillo does not attack players. It responds to threats by rolling up and taking reduced damage.

provocation.answer: Sprinting or mounted players and nearby undead can frighten an armadillo into rolling up; this is defensive behavior, not aggression.

counterplay.answer: Slow down and let it unroll rather than attacking it. Use a brush for scutes; killing it is not the scute-harvesting interaction.

identity.answer: An armadillo is a passive animal that rolls up when it senses certain threats. Collect its scutes, including by brushing it, to make and repair wolf armor.

behavior.answer: An armadillo is a passive animal that rolls up when it senses certain threats. Collect its scutes, including by brushing it, to make and repair wolf armor.

combat.answer: It does not normally attack players. Collect its scutes, including by brushing it, to make and repair wolf armor.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 12 health points (6 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.
Bedrock armor stands have 6 health points (3 hearts). They are display entities, not living animals.

interactions.answer: Armor stands display equipment. In Bedrock you can change their pose and give them held items. Breaking one can drop the stand and its displayed equipment.

drops.answer: Breaking an armor stand can drop the stand item and equipment it displays. Destructive damage such as an explosion can have different results.

equipment.answer: Use armor and held items directly on the stand; it has no ordinary inventory window. Bedrock armor stands have arms and can display held items.

posing.answer: Sneak and interact to cycle supported poses. Redstone can also control poses. This is display behavior, not a living mob’s attack AI.

retrieval.answer: Breaking the stand can release its displayed equipment and the stand item. Fire, explosions or destructive hazards can still destroy items; do not use it as protected backup storage.

identity.answer: An armor stand is a display entity for equipment. Use it to display armor and compatible equipment; Bedrock armor stands support posing and additional held items.

behavior.answer: An armor stand is a display entity for equipment. Use it to display armor and compatible equipment; Bedrock armor stands support posing and additional held items.

spawning.answer: Arrows become projectile entities when fired from a bow, crossbow or dispenser. Skeleton-like mobs also shoot them.

combat.answer: Arrows damage targets they hit. Tipped arrows can also apply their effect; shields and cover can protect against many arrow attacks.

interactions.answer: Some arrows stuck in blocks can be picked up, but arrows shot by mobs and other restricted projectiles are not all recoverable.

projectile_use.answer: Shoot arrows with a bow or crossbow. An arrow lodged in a block can activate supported targets or wooden switches.

projectile_effects.answer: Ordinary arrows can hurt targets; tipped arrows add their own status effects. The effect depends on the ammunition, not only the bow.

retrieval.answer: Some arrows lodged in blocks can be picked up, but mob-fired, Creative and Infinity arrows have pickup restrictions. Do not assume every arrow you see is a recoverable item.

identity.answer: An arrow is ammunition for bows, crossbows, and dispensers. Fire it at a target to deal damage; tipped arrows can also apply effects.

behavior.answer: An arrow is ammunition for bows, crossbows, and dispensers. Fire it at a target to deal damage; tipped arrows can also apply effects.

spawning.answer: Look underwater in lush caves with clay less than five blocks below the spawning space. Blue axolotls come from breeding rather than natural spawning.

drops.answer: Axolotls have no normal item drops. A player or tamed wolf kill can give experience.

breeding.answer: Feed buckets of tropical fish to two adult axolotls. Loose tropical fish items do not work. A baby has a 1 in 1,200 chance to be blue; otherwise it inherits a parent’s color. In Bedrock, the breeding cooldown is one minute.

taming.answer: Axolotls are not tamed. Use a water bucket to collect one and relocate it.

variants.answer: Axolotls come in pink/leucistic, brown, gold, cyan and blue. The first four occur naturally; blue is obtained through breeding rather than natural spawning.

interactions.answer: Axolotls attack many aquatic mobs, can play dead when hurt, and can help a player fighting a shared aquatic target. Keep them wet; being out of water too long is dangerous.

water.answer: Axolotls live underwater and cannot drown normally. A water bucket can safely transport one.

land.answer: Axolotls can spend a limited time on land, but dry out without water or suitable wet conditions. Keep a path back to water or carry one in a water bucket.

fire.answer: Axolotls are not fireproof; lava and fire can kill them.

sunlight.answer: Sunlight alone does not make it burn like an exposed zombie or skeleton. Other hazards, such as being out of water or changing dimensions, can still matter for the species.

age_lock.answer: Use a golden dandelion on an eligible baby to pause its aging. Use another golden dandelion on that same baby to resume aging. This is separate from feeding normal food to speed growth.

spawn_conditions.answer: Check for a lush-caves biome, water and nearby clay below the spawning space. A pond in another biome is not enough. Blue axolotls do not naturally spawn.

leashing.answer: Yes. Use a lead on it to move it, then use a fence to tie it there. You can remove the lead with shears. Leashing does not tame the creature or give it immunity to hazards.

bucketing.answer: Use a water bucket directly on the creature to capture it, then use the filled bucket to release it into suitable water. Capturing and releasing it prevents ordinary natural despawning. A dispenser can release a bucketed creature but does not capture one with a water bucket.

support.answer: When you kill a mob that is fighting your axolotl, it can remove your Mining Fatigue and grant Regeneration. It is not a tamed pet, and the benefit depends on helping with that fight rather than just standing near an axolotl.

playing_dead.answer: An axolotl hurt underwater can play dead briefly and regenerate while hostile aquatic mobs ignore it. It does not do this on every hit, and playing dead is not permanent invulnerability.

experience.answer: An axolotl can give experience after a player or tamed-wolf kill, but I am not sure of the exact amount. Its breeding reward is separate.

experience_baby.answer: A baby axolotl gives no death experience.

experience_breeding.answer: Successful breeding gives 1–7 experience points. That reward comes from breeding, not from killing the baby. The animal’s own breeding requirements still apply.

attack_style.answer: Axolotls hunt fish and several other aquatic mobs, including guardians and drowned. They are passive toward players, but can kill fish in a shared tank.

provocation.answer: An axolotl does not become a player-hunting hostile mob when you approach it. Its hunting behavior targets aquatic prey, with hostile prey prioritized.

counterplay.answer: Keep display fish and tadpoles separate from axolotls. An injured axolotl may play dead underwater, but this is not guaranteed protection against every hit or against drying out.

lifetime.answer: Catching it in a water bucket and releasing it prevents ordinary natural despawning. That does not prevent damage or death. A tadpole can still grow into a frog; capture is not a command to stop aging.

relocation.answer: Capture it with a water bucket, carry the filled bucket, and release it into safe water at the destination. Protect aquatic creatures from dry land. A dispenser can release a filled bucket but cannot catch a creature with a water bucket.

breeding_age.answer: No. A baby cannot breed; it must grow into an adult first. Food that helps it grow is not the same as breeding food being used on an adult.

growth.answer: A baby axolotl normally takes about 20 minutes of active game time to become an adult. You can speed this up by feeding it buckets of tropical fish, not loose tropical fish.

diet.answer: Feed axolotls buckets of tropical fish to breed adults or help babies grow. Loose tropical fish items do not replace the bucket. Axolotls also hunt aquatic mobs such as fish and drowned, which is different from feeding them by hand.

identity.answer: An axolotl is an aquatic animal that can help fight certain underwater mobs. Carry it in a water bucket and use buckets of tropical fish for breeding. It cannot stay out of water indefinitely.

behavior.answer: An axolotl is an aquatic animal that can help fight certain underwater mobs. Carry it in a water bucket and use buckets of tropical fish for breeding. It cannot stay out of water indefinitely.

combat.answer: It does not normally attack players. Carry it in a water bucket and use buckets of tropical fish for breeding. It cannot stay out of water indefinitely.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 14 health points (7 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

identity.answer: This is the pink axolotl color variant.

spawning.answer: Look for pink axolotls in suitable lush-cave water with clay nearby underneath. This is a naturally spawning color, not a separate biome-exclusive species.

variants.answer: Its color does not give it different ordinary health or attack abilities.

identity.answer: This is the brown axolotl color variant.

spawning.answer: Look for brown axolotls in suitable lush-cave water with clay nearby underneath. This is a naturally spawning color, not a separate biome-exclusive species.

variants.answer: Its color does not give it different ordinary health or attack abilities.

identity.answer: This is the gold axolotl color variant.

spawning.answer: Look for gold axolotls in suitable lush-cave water with clay nearby underneath. This is a naturally spawning color, not a separate biome-exclusive species.

variants.answer: Its color does not give it different ordinary health or attack abilities.

identity.answer: This is the cyan axolotl color variant.

spawning.answer: Look for cyan axolotls in suitable lush-cave water with clay nearby underneath. This is a naturally spawning color, not a separate biome-exclusive species.

variants.answer: Its color does not give it different ordinary health or attack abilities.

identity.answer: This is the blue axolotl color variant.

spawning.answer: Blue axolotls do not spawn naturally. Breed adult axolotls using buckets of tropical fish. A baby has a 1-in-1,200 blue-mutation chance; blue parents can also pass their color to offspring.

variants.answer: Its color does not give it different ordinary health or attack abilities.

spawning.answer: Look in roofed dark Overworld spaces, except the deep dark. In Bedrock, bats can spawn at any height on suitable stone-type blocks with light level 4 or less.

drops.answer: Bats drop no items or experience when killed.

breeding.answer: Bats cannot be bred.

taming.answer: Bats cannot be tamed or trained to follow a player.

interactions.answer: Bats are ambient animals. They fly around and hang from blocks, but are not a source of useful loot.

fire.answer: Without protection, it can take fire and lava damage and die. Living in a warm biome or having a particular coat color does not grant fire immunity.

sunlight.answer: Ordinary sunlight does not make this creature spontaneously burn. Fire, lava and lightning are separate hazards.

land.answer: It can live on land. Still provide suitable safe terrain and protect it from fire, falls or other species-specific hazards.

variants.answer: A hanging bat and a flying bat are the same creature in different behavior states.

spawn_conditions.answer: Check light level 4 or less, no direct sky exposure, enough air space, and stone, granite, diorite, andesite, tuff or deepslate below. Bats have an ambient population cap; a low cave height alone is not the deciding condition.

leashing.answer: No, you cannot attach an ordinary lead to it through normal player interaction.

experience.answer: It gives no experience when killed. Item drops and rewards from other interactions are separate.

growth.answer: A bat has no normal baby form that grows into an adult. There is no ordinary baby-growth timer or growth food to use for this mob.

lifetime.answer: A naturally spawned bat can disappear through ordinary distance despawning unless it has become persistent. In Bedrock, a name tag is one way to prevent ordinary distance despawning; distance rules depend on simulation settings and mob state. A boat or minecart alone is not a blanket persistence guarantee, and persistence does not prevent death.

relocation.answer: A minecart can carry a bat in Bedrock. Bring an empty cart into contact with it, then use rails and powered rails along a protected route. An active activator rail can eject the passenger. The cart alone does not guarantee persistence in Bedrock.

attack_style.answer: Bats do not attack players or inflict melee damage. Their erratic flying is not a charge attack.

provocation.answer: A disturbed bat flies away instead of fighting back. It cannot be turned into a guard pet by provoking or taming it.

counterplay.answer: No combat counter is needed for a bat. It is a passive cave animal; avoid confusing its flight with a nearby hostile mob.

identity.answer: A bat is a small passive flying cave animal. It adds atmosphere to dark areas and is not a tameable companion or a useful loot source.

behavior.answer: A bat is a small passive flying cave animal. It adds atmosphere to dark areas and is not a tameable companion or a useful loot source.

combat.answer: It does not normally attack players. It adds atmosphere to dark areas and is not a tameable companion or a useful loot source.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 6 health points (3 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

fall_damage.answer: It does not take ordinary fall damage. Other damage sources can still hurt it.

spawning.answer: Find bees inside naturally generated bee nests on trees. Flower-rich biomes such as meadows are useful places to search. Growing suitable trees can also produce nests with bees.

drops.answer: Bees do not normally drop items on death. Adults can give experience. Honey bottles and honeycomb are harvested from a full nest or hive, not from killing bees.

breeding.answer: Feed suitable flowers to two adult bees. Do not use wither roses or eyeblossoms for breeding. Bees have a breeding cooldown, and time spent working inside a hive pauses their growth and breeding timers.

taming.answer: Bees cannot be tamed. Flowers attract them, and a suitable nest or hive provides a home.

interactions.answer: Bees pollinate flowers and return to their home to make honey. Harvest a full hive with bottles for honey or shears for honeycomb. A correctly placed campfire can calm the hive while harvesting. Attacking bees or disturbing an unprotected hive can provoke them.

fire.answer: Without protection, it can take fire and lava damage and die. Living in a warm biome or having a particular coat color does not grant fire immunity.

sunlight.answer: Ordinary sunlight does not make this creature spontaneously burn. Fire, lava and lightning are separate hazards.

harvesting.answer: At honey level five, use shears for honeycomb or a glass bottle for honey. A lit campfire below the nest or hive can prevent harvesting anger if the smoke reaches it. Protect bees from touching the fire. Breaking the hive is different from harvesting its honey.

anger.answer: Attacking bees or disturbing a hive without the required protection can anger them. A suitable lit campfire helps with harvesting but is not a universal shield against every provocation.

land.answer: It can live on land. Still provide suitable safe terrain and protect it from fire, falls or other species-specific hazards.

age_lock.answer: Use a golden dandelion on an eligible baby to pause its aging. Use another golden dandelion on that same baby to resume aging. This is separate from feeding normal food to speed growth.

variants.answer: Bees have baby and adult stages. Anger and carrying nectar or pollen are changing states, not different breeds.

spawn_conditions.answer: Bees come with generated nests rather than randomly appearing around a crafted empty beehive. Growing oak, birch or cherry saplings within two blocks of suitable flowers has a chance to produce a populated nest; a single tree is not guaranteed to do so.

leashing.answer: Yes. Use a lead on it to move it, then use a fence to tie it there. You can remove the lead with shears. Leashing does not tame the creature or give it immunity to hazards.

pollination.answer: A nectar-carrying bee can help supported crops grow when it flies one or two blocks above them and has a valid home hive. It does not plant seeds or harvest the crop for you. Flowers supply nectar; a crafted empty hive alone does not supply bees.

experience.answer: An adult can drop 1–3 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Babies do not give death experience. These are experience points, not player levels.

experience_baby.answer: The baby does not give experience when killed. Growing into an adult changes its death reward; it is separate from experience earned by successful breeding.

experience_breeding.answer: Successful breeding gives 1–7 experience points. That reward comes from breeding, not from killing the baby. The animal’s own breeding requirements still apply.

attack_style.answer: An angry bee approaches and stings. Other nearby bees can join the attack.

provocation.answer: Attacking bees, destroying their home or harvesting honey without suitable smoke can anger them. Hitting a hive and breaking it are different actions.

counterplay.answer: Avoid provoking the colony. Use a correctly placed lit campfire for honey harvesting and protect bees from the flames. Smoke is not a blanket guarantee against every other provocation.

breeding_age.answer: No. A baby cannot breed; it must grow into an adult first. Food that helps it grow is not the same as breeding food being used on an adult.

growth.answer: A baby bee normally takes about 20 minutes of active game time to become an adult. You can speed this up by feeding it a suitable flower such as a dandelion or poppy. Its growth timer pauses while it is inside a nest or hive.

diet.answer: Suitable flowers such as dandelions and poppies let you breed adult bees or help babies grow. Bees also visit flowers to collect pollen; pollination and feeding are different interactions. Avoid wither roses and poisonous eyeblossoms.

lifetime.answer: Tempting a bee with suitable flowers or breeding it gives it persistence in Bedrock. Protect the bee and its hive as well: persistence does not stop damage or keep it from flying away.

relocation.answer: You can use a lead to move a bee. Guide it along a safe route, keep it close enough that the lead does not break, and protect it from falls and unsuitable water or heat.

identity.answer: A bee is a flying animal that visits flowers and returns to a nest or hive. It helps produce honey and can pollinate crops. Disturbing bees or harvesting carelessly can make them attack.

behavior.answer: A bee is a flying animal that visits flowers and returns to a nest or hive. It helps produce honey and can pollinate crops. Disturbing bees or harvesting carelessly can make them attack.

combat.answer: It can attack under particular conditions, so do not assume it is always harmless. It helps produce honey and can pollinate crops. Disturbing bees or harvesting carelessly can make them attack.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 10 health points (5 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

fall_damage.answer: It does not take ordinary fall damage. Other damage sources can still hurt it.

withheld.name: wither rose
withheld.answer: I'm not sure whether wither roses are suitable for bees. Use a flower such as a dandelion or poppy instead.

spawning.answer: Look in Nether fortresses, especially at blaze-spawner platforms. Blazes can also spawn naturally within fortress spawning areas.

drops.answer: A blaze can drop 0–1 blaze rods when killed by a player or tamed wolf; Looting can increase the amount. Environmental kills do not provide the normal blaze-rod drop.

combat.answer: Blazes shoot bursts of fireballs and can attack up close. They resist fire and lava, but water and snowballs hurt them. Fire resistance helps against burning, not every kind of damage.

taming.answer: Blaze cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: You cannot breed a blaze.

water.answer: Water damages blazes. Rain can also hurt an exposed blaze outside its normal Nether environment.

rain.answer: Rain can damage an exposed blaze. Nether fortresses do not naturally have ordinary rain.

powder_snow.answer: Blazes take extra freezing damage from powder snow despite being immune to fire.

variants.answer: A blaze that is preparing to shoot is in an attack state. A breeze is a different mob, not another blaze color.

spawn_conditions.answer: Blazes require light level 11 or less. Natural fortress spawning depends on the fortress piece or overall fortress bounds; in the larger fortress bounds, Nether bricks are required. Spawner spawning is a separate route, so an ordinary Nether-brick platform outside a fortress is not enough.

experience.answer: It gives 10 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Looting affects certain item drops, not this experience reward.

attack_style.answer: A blaze launches small fireballs that can ignite its target, and can hurt you at close range. Its fireballs differ from the large ghast fireballs.

provocation.answer: Blazes are hostile and can attack without being hit first. They are immune to fire, so fire and lava are not useful ways to defeat them.

counterplay.answer: Use cover between bursts. A shield can block the fireball damage and ignition. Snowballs can damage blazes; Fire Resistance helps against fire but does not make every close-range hit harmless.

growth.answer: A blaze has no normal baby form that grows into an adult. There is no ordinary baby-growth timer or growth food to use for this mob.

lifetime.answer: A naturally spawned blaze can disappear through ordinary distance despawning unless it has become persistent. In Bedrock, a name tag is one way to prevent ordinary distance despawning; distance rules depend on simulation settings and mob state. A boat or minecart alone is not a blanket persistence guarantee, and persistence does not prevent death.

relocation.answer: A minecart can carry a blaze in Bedrock. Bring an empty cart into contact with it, then use rails and powered rails along a protected route. An active activator rail can eject the passenger. It can still be dangerous while riding; a cart is not taming or protection from its attacks. The cart alone does not guarantee persistence in Bedrock.

identity.answer: A blaze is a flying hostile Nether mob that attacks with fireballs. Fight it carefully to obtain blaze rods, which are important for brewing and eyes of ender.

behavior.answer: A blaze is a flying hostile Nether mob that attacks with fireballs. Fight it carefully to obtain blaze rods, which are important for brewing and eyes of ender.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 20 health points (10 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

fire.answer: It is immune to ordinary fire and lava damage. That does not protect it from every other kind of damage.

sunlight.answer: Ordinary sunlight does not make it take burning damage. It is fire-immune, although other environmental hazards can still matter.

fall_damage.answer: It does not take ordinary fall damage. Other damage sources can still hurt it.

spawning.answer: Place a boat item on suitable water or ground to create the boat entity.

transport.answer: Use a boat to travel over water and carry up to two passengers. Ice also allows fast boat travel. Boats are not tamed or bred.

drops.answer: A normally broken boat drops its boat item. Destruction by fire or other hazards can have different results.

storage.answer: An ordinary boat has two rider positions. Many land mobs can ride, but a hostile passenger can still attack. A boat with chest has different capacity.

propulsion.answer: Enter and use the movement controls to paddle. Boats can be leashed for towing; they are not lava-proof vehicles.

retrieval.answer: Breaking a boat returns its boat item under ordinary conditions and releases passengers. Moving a mob into a boat is not a universal way to cancel special despawn timers.

identity.answer: A boat is a rideable vehicle for travelling across water. Place it on water, board it, and steer; it can also carry suitable passengers.

behavior.answer: A boat is a rideable vehicle for travelling across water. Place it on water, board it, and steer; it can also carry suitable passengers.

spawning.answer: Find bogged on the surface in swamps and mangrove swamps, or from certain trial-chamber spawners.

drops.answer: Bogged can drop bones, arrows and, under player or tamed-wolf kill conditions, an arrow of poison. Equipment has separate drop conditions. Shearing a bogged gives two mushrooms once; those are not its ordinary death drops.

interactions.answer: Use shears to remove its mushrooms once. Bogged shoot poison arrows, so keep cover between you and them.

taming.answer: Bogged cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: You cannot breed a bogged.

shearing.answer: Shearing a bogged removes its mushrooms and gives two mushrooms once. That harvest is separate from its ordinary kill loot.

fire.answer: Without protection, ordinary fire and lava can damage it. Being undead, large, or adapted to a particular biome does not by itself grant fire immunity.

variants.answer: Bogged can have mushrooms or be sheared. They are a separate skeleton-type mob rather than a baby skeleton.

spawn_conditions.answer: Bedrock natural bogged spawning is surface-only, at light levels 0–7 in swamps or mangrove swamps. A dark underground swamp cave is not the same route. Trial spawners are separate and must have bogged selected as their mob.

experience.answer: The base reward is 5 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Naturally spawned equipment can affect the total; picked-up equipment and whether the gear itself drops are separate conditions. Looting does not multiply experience.

equipment_drops.answer: Naturally spawned weapons or armor are not guaranteed drops. Qualifying player or tamed-wolf kills and Looting can matter. Equipment the mob picked up later is a different category; do not assume one chance covers both. Its ordinary body loot is separate.

attack_style.answer: A bogged uses a bow and can inflict Poison with its arrows. Shearing its mushrooms does not remove its ability to attack.

provocation.answer: Bogged are hostile skeleton-type mobs. Removing their head mushrooms is a harvesting action, not taming or disarming.

counterplay.answer: Use cover and a shield against arrows. Poison management does not replace avoiding the next shot; shearing one does not make it safe.

growth.answer: A bogged has no normal baby form that grows into an adult. There is no ordinary baby-growth timer or growth food to use for this mob.

lifetime.answer: A naturally spawned bogged can disappear through ordinary distance despawning unless it has become persistent. In Bedrock, a name tag is one way to prevent ordinary distance despawning; distance rules depend on simulation settings and mob state. A boat or minecart alone is not a blanket persistence guarantee, and persistence does not prevent death.

relocation.answer: A minecart can carry a bogged in Bedrock. Bring an empty cart into contact with it, then use rails and powered rails along a protected route. An active activator rail can eject the passenger. It can still be dangerous while riding; a cart is not taming or protection from its attacks. The cart alone does not guarantee persistence in Bedrock.

identity.answer: A bogged is a skeleton-like hostile mob that fires poisoned arrows. Use cover against its ranged attacks; shearing it can remove its mushrooms.

behavior.answer: A bogged is a skeleton-like hostile mob that fires poisoned arrows. Use cover against its ranged attacks; shearing it can remove its mushrooms.

combat.answer: It is a hostile mob and can attack players. Use cover against its ranged attacks; shearing it can remove its mushrooms.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 16 health points (8 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

sunlight.answer: It can burn in direct sunlight when unprotected. Shade, water and applicable armor protection can prevent that; sunlight protection does not make it immune to lava.

water.answer: It can breathe underwater.

spawning.answer: Look for breeze trial spawners in trial-chamber combat rooms, commonly surrounded by chiseled tuff. Breezes do not naturally wander around ordinary caves.

drops.answer: A breeze killed by a player or tamed wolf drops 1–2 breeze rods; Looting can increase the amount.

combat.answer: A breeze jumps around and fires wind charges that push targets and activate some mechanisms. It deflects many projectiles, so do not assume arrows are a reliable counter. Watch your landing after a wind burst.

taming.answer: Breeze cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: You cannot breed a breeze.

sunlight.answer: Sunlight alone does not make it burn like an exposed zombie or skeleton. Other hazards, such as being out of water or changing dimensions, can still matter for the species.

fire.answer: Without protection, ordinary fire and lava can damage it. Being undead, large, or adapted to a particular biome does not by itself grant fire immunity.

variants.answer: Breezes and blazes are different mobs. A breeze changing its pose while jumping or attacking is not changing species.

spawn_conditions.answer: Use a breeze-configured trial spawner in a trial-chamber combat room. It needs a valid spawn position with line of sight to the spawner. A normal dark platform or an unrelated trial spawner does not produce breezes.

experience.answer: It gives 10 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Looting affects certain item drops, not this experience reward.

attack_style.answer: A breeze jumps around and fires wind charges that knock targets around and can activate nearby mechanisms.

provocation.answer: Breezes are hostile trial-chamber mobs. They automatically deflect most direct projectiles, so firing ordinary arrows is not a reliable solution.

counterplay.answer: Use cover and watch your footing. Melee attacks or wind charges are useful options because ordinary direct projectiles are deflected. Area effects from splash potions differ from direct projectile hits.

growth.answer: A breeze has no normal baby form that grows into an adult. There is no ordinary baby-growth timer or growth food to use for this mob.

lifetime.answer: Breezes normally have persistence in Bedrock and do not disappear through ordinary distance despawning. They can still be killed or removed by other game rules.

relocation.answer: A minecart can carry a breeze in Bedrock. Bring an empty cart into contact with it, then use rails and powered rails along a protected route. An active activator rail can eject the passenger. It can still be dangerous while riding; a cart is not taming or protection from its attacks. The cart alone does not guarantee persistence in Bedrock.

identity.answer: A breeze is a jumping hostile mob found in trial chambers. It fires wind charges that knock entities around and interact with certain mechanisms. Its drops are used in wind-related crafting.

behavior.answer: A breeze is a jumping hostile mob found in trial chambers. It fires wind charges that knock entities around and interact with certain mechanisms. Its drops are used in wind-related crafting.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 30 health points (15 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

fall_damage.answer: It does not take ordinary fall damage. Other damage sources can still hurt it.

spawning.answer: Wind-charge projectiles come from breezes or from using a wind charge item, depending on the projectile type.

interactions.answer: Wind charges burst on impact, pushing entities and interacting with some buttons, doors and other mechanisms. Player wind charges and breeze projectiles do not have identical rules.

projectile_use.answer: A breeze fires this wind-charge projectile as its ranged attack. It differs from the wind-charge item a player throws.

projectile_effects.answer: Its wind burst pushes entities and can trigger supported mechanisms. Keep footing and nearby machinery in mind.

retrieval.answer: You cannot collect the breeze’s fired projectile as the player’s wind-charge item.

identity.answer: A breeze wind charge is the projectile fired by a breeze. Its wind burst can knock entities around and activate certain blocks when it hits.

behavior.answer: A breeze wind charge is the projectile fired by a breeze. Its wind burst can knock entities around and activate certain blocks when it hits.

spawning.answer: Look in deserts and desert villages. A camel can be generated in the center of a non-abandoned desert village.

drops.answer: Camels do not have a normal meat or leather drop. An equipped saddle can drop when the camel dies; adults can give experience in Bedrock.

breeding.answer: Feed cactus to two adult camels. The baby grows over time and cactus can help it grow.

taming.answer: Camels do not require taming. Equip an adult with a saddle to control it.

transport.answer: A saddled adult camel can carry two players and dash forward. Its height puts riders above the reach of some short melee attackers, but does not make riders safe from every attack.

fire.answer: Without protection, it can take fire and lava damage and die. Living in a warm biome or having a particular coat color does not grant fire immunity.

sunlight.answer: Ordinary sunlight does not make this creature spontaneously burn. Fire, lava and lightning are separate hazards.

water.answer: It needs air and can drown if trapped fully underwater. Being able to swim or float is not the same as being able to breathe underwater.

powder_snow.answer: It can take freezing damage while trapped in powder snow without applicable protection. A cold-biome home or white coat alone does not guarantee freezing immunity.

equipment.answer: A saddle lets you control an adult camel. It can carry two players; it does not require horse-style taming.

land.answer: It can live on land. Still provide suitable safe terrain and protect it from fire, falls or other species-specific hazards.

age_lock.answer: Use a golden dandelion on an eligible baby to pause its aging. Use another golden dandelion on that same baby to resume aging. This is separate from feeding normal food to speed growth.

variants.answer: Camels have baby and adult stages. A camel husk is a separate undead mob, not an adult stage of an ordinary camel.

spawn_conditions.answer: Camels can appear in deserts, including the original camel generated in a non-abandoned desert village. Clearing or rebuilding a village does not regenerate that original camel. Ordinary natural spawning and the village-generated camel are separate sources.

leashing.answer: Yes. Use a lead on it to move it, then use a fence to tie it there. You can remove the lead with shears. Leashing does not tame the creature or give it immunity to hazards.

experience.answer: An adult can drop 1–3 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Babies do not give death experience. These are experience points, not player levels.

experience_baby.answer: The baby does not give experience when killed. Growing into an adult changes its death reward; it is separate from experience earned by successful breeding.

experience_breeding.answer: Successful breeding gives 1–7 experience points. That reward comes from breeding, not from killing the baby. The animal’s own breeding requirements still apply.

relocation.answer: Equip an adult camel with a saddle for controlled riding. It can carry two players; sitting and standing are different movement states. A lead can guide it without riding.

breeding_age.answer: No. A baby cannot breed; it must grow into an adult first. Food that helps it grow is not the same as breeding food being used on an adult.

growth.answer: A baby camel normally takes about 20 minutes of active game time to become an adult. You can speed this up by feeding it cactus.

diet.answer: Cactus can heal camels, help baby camels grow and breed adults. Camels can be ridden without taming, so cactus is not a taming requirement.

lifetime.answer: A naturally spawned camel can disappear through ordinary distance despawning unless it has become persistent. In Bedrock, a name tag is one way to prevent ordinary distance despawning; distance rules depend on simulation settings and mob state. Suitable player interactions, such as breeding, tempting with accepted food or leashing where supported, can also give persistence. A boat or minecart alone is not a blanket persistence guarantee, and persistence does not prevent death.

attack_style.answer: A camel does not attack players on its own. A rider using a weapon is a separate source of damage.

provocation.answer: A camel is passive and does not retaliate against a player like a neutral wolf. Its dash is a movement ability, not a command to attack.

counterplay.answer: Treat a rider and its mount separately. For your own camel, use a saddle and safe routes rather than trying to make it a combat pet.

identity.answer: A camel is a tall rideable desert animal. Use a saddle to ride it with up to two players, and use its dash to cross suitable gaps.

behavior.answer: A camel is a tall rideable desert animal. Use a saddle to ride it with up to two players, and use its dash to cross suitable gaps.

combat.answer: It does not normally attack players. Use a saddle to ride it with up to two players, and use its dash to cross suitable gaps.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 32 health points (16 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

spawning.answer: Camel husks appear in deserts as jockeys with hostile passengers. In Bedrock these jockeys can appear at night or during thunderstorms; their passengers and mount are separate entities.

drops.answer: A camel husk normally drops 2–3 rotten flesh, plus applicable equipped items. Killing its passengers and killing the mount are separate events with separate loot.

breeding.answer: Camel husks cannot be bred like living camels.

interactions.answer: The mount does not attack like its hostile passengers. Deal with each rider separately; removing a rider does not automatically kill the camel husk.

taming.answer: Camel husk cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

combat.answer: The camel husk itself is passive, but its hostile passengers can make the whole jockey dangerous. Removing a rider does not automatically remove the mount or the other rider.

sunlight.answer: Sunlight alone does not make it burn like an exposed zombie or skeleton. Other hazards, such as being out of water or changing dimensions, can still matter for the species.

fire.answer: Without protection, ordinary fire and lava can damage it. Being undead, large, or adapted to a particular biome does not by itself grant fire immunity.

variants.answer: A camel husk is an undead mount. Its riders are separate mobs, not part of a single combined creature.

spawn_conditions.answer: Bedrock camel husks use desert monster spawning and appear with riders, not as ordinary passive desert camels. They do not naturally spawn in Peaceful.

leashing.answer: You can attach a lead once it is not being ridden by a hostile mob. Deal with the hostile rider first; the mount and rider are separate creatures.

experience.answer: A camel husk gives 1–3 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. The mount and any riders are separate mobs with separate rewards.

lifetime.answer: A camel husk can despawn before player interaction makes it persistent. Riding it makes it persistent. Any hostile riders are separate mobs, and the mount’s persistence does not make the riders friendly.

diet.answer: A rabbit’s foot can tempt and heal a camel husk. This undead mount does not use the cactus feeding interaction of an ordinary camel.

growth.answer: A camel husk has no normal baby form that grows into an adult. There is no ordinary baby-growth timer or growth food to use for this mob.

relocation.answer: You can use a lead to move a camel husk. Guide it along a safe route, keep it close enough that the lead does not break, and protect it from falls and unsuitable water or heat. Remove hostile riders before trying to attach the lead; a hostile rider is a separate opponent.

attack_style.answer: The camel husk itself is passive, but its hostile passengers can attack while riding it. The mount and each rider are separate entities.

provocation.answer: A camel husk jockey is dangerous because hostile riders control the encounter, not because the bare mount has become an ordinary player-hunting attacker.

counterplay.answer: Deal with the hostile riders before handling the mount, and do not assume removing one passenger removes every attacker. A rabbit’s foot can heal the mount once safe to approach.

identity.answer: A camel husk is an undead camel variant. It can carry riders, including hostile ones under suitable conditions. Its undead behavior differs from an ordinary camel.

behavior.answer: A camel husk is an undead camel variant. It can carry riders, including hostile ones under suitable conditions. Its undead behavior differs from an ordinary camel.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 32 health points (16 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

water.answer: It can breathe underwater. It can also breathe air.

spawning.answer: Find cats in villages and a black cat at a swamp hut. Bedrock village cats depend on claimed beds and the number of cats already in the village.

drops.answer: Adult cats can drop 0–2 string. Babies have no normal item or experience drops. Gifts brought by a tamed cat after you sleep are a separate mechanic.

breeding.answer: Feed raw cod or raw salmon to two tamed adult cats. Two sitting cats cannot breed; let at least one move toward the other.

taming.answer: Approach an untamed cat carefully and feed raw cod or raw salmon. It may take multiple fish. Once tamed it can follow you or be told to sit.

health.answer: In Bedrock, wild cats have 10 health points (5 hearts), while tamed cats have 20 health points (10 hearts).

interactions.answer: Cats scare creepers and phantoms. You can dye a tamed cat’s collar and tell it to sit or follow. A tamed cat may bring a gift after sleeping near its owner.

variants.answer: Cats have eleven coat variants: all black, british shorthair, calico, jellie, persian, ragdoll, red, siamese, tabby, tuxedo, white. Collar dye changes a tamed cat’s collar, not its coat.

fire.answer: Without protection, it can take fire and lava damage and die. Living in a warm biome or having a particular coat color does not grant fire immunity.

sunlight.answer: Ordinary sunlight does not make this creature spontaneously burn. Fire, lava and lightning are separate hazards.

water.answer: It needs air and can drown if trapped fully underwater. Being able to swim or float is not the same as being able to breathe underwater.

powder_snow.answer: It can take freezing damage while trapped in powder snow without applicable protection. A cold-biome home or white coat alone does not guarantee freezing immunity.

sleeping.answer: A tamed cat can rest near its owner and may bring a gift after the owner sleeps. That gift mechanic is separate from killing a cat for drops.

land.answer: It can live on land. Still provide suitable safe terrain and protect it from fire, falls or other species-specific hazards.

age_lock.answer: Use a golden dandelion on an eligible baby to pause its aging. Use another golden dandelion on that same baby to resume aging. This is separate from feeding normal food to speed growth.

spawn_conditions.answer: Bedrock villages try to fill a quota of one cat per four claimed beds, up to five cats at 20 or more claimed beds. Existing cats, including babies and tamed visitors, count toward the quota. Provide a valid spawning space near the village center; merely placing unclaimed beds is not enough.

leashing.answer: Yes. Use a lead on it to move it, then use a fence to tie it there. You can remove the lead with shears. Leashing does not tame the creature or give it immunity to hazards.

sitting.answer: As its owner, use the tamed creature to switch between sitting and standing. Sitting keeps it from normally following you; it does not grant invulnerability. Use an empty hand to avoid a food or equipment interaction instead.

defense.answer: Cats repel creepers and phantoms, but do not make you immune to them. A creeper already beginning its explosion may not flee, so move out of its blast range rather than relying on the cat.

collar.answer: After taming a cat, its owner can use dye to recolor its collar. Dye does not change the cat’s coat pattern.

experience.answer: An adult can drop 1–3 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Babies do not give death experience. These are experience points, not player levels.

experience_baby.answer: The baby does not give experience when killed. Growing into an adult changes its death reward; it is separate from experience earned by successful breeding.

experience_breeding.answer: Successful breeding gives 1–7 experience points. That reward comes from breeding, not from killing the baby. The animal’s own breeding requirements still apply.

lifetime.answer: A tamed cat does not naturally despawn. Stray cats can have different persistence depending on how they spawned; the original swamp-hut cat is persistent. Tame the cat you want to keep and protect it from hazards.

relocation.answer: Tame it, tell it to stand and let it follow, or use a lead. A sitting cat is not following. Provide safe footing and do not rely on pet teleporting to prevent every travel accident.

teleportation.answer: A tamed pet that is standing can follow and teleport closer when far enough away if a valid destination is available. Sitting and other travel states can prevent normal following. Do not assume it can teleport out of an unloaded area or automatically cross dimensions; move carefully and check it arrives.

breeding_age.answer: No. A baby cannot breed; it must grow into an adult first. Food that helps it grow is not the same as breeding food being used on an adult.

breeding_ownership.answer: The parents must be tamed before breeding. Use eligible adult animals and their breeding food; feeding wild animals is not enough to skip taming.

growth.answer: A baby cat normally takes about 20 minutes of active game time to become an adult. You can speed this up by feeding it raw cod or raw salmon.

diet.answer: Raw cod and raw salmon are useful for cats. They can tame a stray cat, heal a cat, help kittens grow and breed tamed adults when the breeding requirements are met. Cooked fish is not a substitute for the raw fish used to tame cats.

attack_style.answer: Cats do not attack players. They hunt small prey such as chickens, rabbits and baby turtles, so a pet cat is not harmless to every animal.

provocation.answer: A cat does not become a player-hunting enemy when hit; it flees. Creepers and phantoms avoid cats rather than being killed by cat attacks.

counterplay.answer: Keep vulnerable small animals separate from cats. Tame a stray with raw fish instead of fighting it, and do not expect a cat to defend you like a wolf.

identity.answer: A cat is a tameable animal often found around villages. Tame it with suitable raw fish to gain a companion. Cats also help keep creepers away.

behavior.answer: A cat is a tameable animal often found around villages. Tame it with suitable raw fish to gain a companion. Cats also help keep creepers away.

combat.answer: It does not normally attack players. Tame it with suitable raw fish to gain a companion. Cats also help keep creepers away.

fall_damage.answer: It does not take ordinary fall damage. Other damage sources can still hurt it.

identity.answer: This is the all black cat coat.

spawning.answer: Look in swamp huts for all-black cats. They can also occur with village cat spawning.

variants.answer: The coat and the owner-dyed collar are separate features.

identity.answer: This is the british shorthair cat coat.

spawning.answer: Look for british shorthair cats among village cats where the bed-related spawning rules are met. This coat is not tied to its own special biome.

variants.answer: The coat and the owner-dyed collar are separate features.

identity.answer: This is the calico cat coat.

spawning.answer: Look for calico cats among village cats where the bed-related spawning rules are met. This coat is not tied to its own special biome.

identity.answer: This is the red cat coat.

spawning.answer: Look for red cats among village cats where the bed-related spawning rules are met. This coat is not tied to its own special biome.

identity.answer: This is the siamese cat coat.

spawning.answer: Look for siamese cats among village cats where the bed-related spawning rules are met. This coat is not tied to its own special biome.

identity.answer: This is the tuxedo cat coat.

spawning.answer: Look for tuxedo cats among village cats where the bed-related spawning rules are met. This coat is not tied to its own special biome.

identity.answer: This is the white cat coat.

spawning.answer: Look for white cats among village cats where the bed-related spawning rules are met. This coat is not tied to its own special biome.

variants.answer: The coat and the owner-dyed collar are separate features.

spawning.answer: Look for cave-spider spawners in cobweb-filled mineshaft corridors and suitable trial spawners. The archived newer rules also include sulfur-cave spawning; that depends on the features present in your game version.

drops.answer: Cave spiders can drop 0–2 string. A player kill can also produce a spider eye, with Looting affecting applicable drops.

combat.answer: Cave spiders are small climbers and their bites can poison you on applicable difficulties. They fit through openings that stop larger mobs, so use a secure barrier rather than a narrow gap.

taming.answer: Cave spider cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: You cannot breed a cave spider.

sunlight.answer: Sunlight alone does not make it burn like an exposed zombie or skeleton. Other hazards, such as being out of water or changing dimensions, can still matter for the species.

fire.answer: Without protection, ordinary fire and lava can damage it. Being undead, large, or adapted to a particular biome does not by itself grant fire immunity.

variants.answer: Cave spiders and regular spiders are separate mobs. A spider jockey consists of a spider and a separate rider.

spawn_conditions.answer: Mineshaft cave-spider spawners require darkness and usable spawning space. Certain trial spawners can also select cave spiders. Natural cave spiders replace ordinary spiders in sulfur caves; an ordinary dark cave in another biome is not the same route.

experience.answer: It gives 5 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Looting affects certain item drops, not this experience reward.

attack_style.answer: A cave spider bites at close range and can climb walls and fit through smaller gaps than an ordinary spider. Its bite applies Poison on Normal and Hard, not Easy.

provocation.answer: It behaves similarly to a spider, with close-range attacks. Do not assume a small gap that blocks ordinary spiders will keep it out.

counterplay.answer: Keep your distance from mineshaft webs and narrow openings. Milk can remove Poison but does not prevent another bite from poisoning you again.

growth.answer: A cave spider has no normal baby form that grows into an adult. There is no ordinary baby-growth timer or growth food to use for this mob.

lifetime.answer: A naturally spawned cave spider can disappear through ordinary distance despawning unless it has become persistent. In Bedrock, a name tag is one way to prevent ordinary distance despawning; distance rules depend on simulation settings and mob state. A boat or minecart alone is not a blanket persistence guarantee, and persistence does not prevent death.

relocation.answer: A minecart can carry a cave spider in Bedrock. Bring an empty cart into contact with it, then use rails and powered rails along a protected route. An active activator rail can eject the passenger. It can still be dangerous while riding; a cart is not taming or protection from its attacks. The cart alone does not guarantee persistence in Bedrock.

identity.answer: A cave spider is a small hostile spider associated with abandoned mineshafts. Its attacks can poison players under suitable difficulty settings. Keep distance and watch for webs.

behavior.answer: A cave spider is a small hostile spider associated with abandoned mineshafts. Its attacks can poison players under suitable difficulty settings. Keep distance and watch for webs.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 12 health points (6 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

spawning.answer: Place a boat-with-chest item to create a storage boat.

transport.answer: A boat with a chest carries one passenger and a storage inventory. Use it to move supplies over water.

drops.answer: Breaking a boat with a chest drops its item and stored contents.

storage.answer: A boat with chest has a single-chest-sized inventory and only one rider position because the chest occupies the other seat. Hoppers can load or unload it.

propulsion.answer: It paddles like a boat. Sneak and interact to access the chest from outside, or open the inventory while riding.

retrieval.answer: Breaking it drops the carried inventory; do not treat it as a protected storage backup. Opening or breaking it near piglins can provoke them.

identity.answer: A chest boat is a boat with built-in item storage. Use it to transport yourself and supplies across water; its chest takes the place of an extra passenger seat.

behavior.answer: A chest boat is a boat with built-in item storage. Use it to transport yourself and supplies across water; its chest takes the place of an extra passenger seat.

spawning.answer: Loot-filled chest minecarts generate in mineshafts. You can also place a crafted chest minecart on rails.

transport.answer: A chest minecart carries a storage inventory along rails. It does not carry a player in its chest space.

drops.answer: Breaking a chest minecart normally drops the chest-minecart item and its stored contents.

storage.answer: A chest minecart provides 27 inventory slots. Hoppers below can remove cargo and suitable hoppers can load it; the cart is storage rather than a passenger seat.

propulsion.answer: It moves along rails like a minecart. Powered rails are useful for maintaining motion; filling it with cargo changes its travel behavior.

retrieval.answer: Destroying it drops the cart and stored items. Plan an unloading station instead of assuming it automatically pushes cargo into every nearby chest.

identity.answer: A chest minecart is a rail vehicle with item storage. Use it to carry supplies along tracks and connect it to loading or unloading systems.

behavior.answer: A chest minecart is a rail vehicle with item storage. Use it to carry supplies along tracks and connect it to loading or unloading systems.

spawning.answer: Chickens appear on grass in many Overworld biomes. They can also hatch from thrown eggs or come from breeding. The variant of a naturally spawned chicken depends on the biome’s climate.

drops.answer: Adult chickens can drop feathers and raw chicken, or cooked chicken if killed while burning. Laying eggs is a separate periodic activity of living adult chickens.

breeding.answer: Feed suitable seeds to two adult chickens, such as wheat, beetroot, melon, pumpkin or torchflower seeds. Pitcher pods also work. A chick inherits a parent’s variant.

interactions.answer: Living adult chickens periodically lay eggs. Throwing an egg can hatch chicks, but does not guarantee one. Chickens fall slowly rather than taking normal fall damage.

taming.answer: Chicken cannot be tamed as player-owned pets. You can still ask how to breed them.

variants.answer: Chickens have temperate, warm and cold forms. Natural spawning chooses the form from the biome; breeding inherits a parent’s form, and moving an adult does not recolor it.

fire.answer: Without protection, it can take fire and lava damage and die. Living in a warm biome or having a particular coat color does not grant fire immunity.

sunlight.answer: Ordinary sunlight does not make this creature spontaneously burn. Fire, lava and lightning are separate hazards.

water.answer: It needs air and can drown if trapped fully underwater. Being able to swim or float is not the same as being able to breathe underwater.

powder_snow.answer: It can take freezing damage while trapped in powder snow without applicable protection. A cold-biome home or white coat alone does not guarantee freezing immunity.

land.answer: It can live on land. Still provide suitable safe terrain and protect it from fire, falls or other species-specific hazards.

age_lock.answer: Use a golden dandelion on an eligible baby to pause its aging. Use another golden dandelion on that same baby to resume aging. This is separate from feeding normal food to speed growth.

spawn_conditions.answer: Bedrock natural chickens need grass blocks and light level 7 or more in an eligible biome. Snowy plains, meadows, cherry groves, mangrove swamps and pale gardens are excluded. Egg hatching and breeding are separate ways to obtain chickens.

leashing.answer: Yes. Use a lead on it to move it, then use a fence to tie it there. You can remove the lead with shears. Leashing does not tame the creature or give it immunity to hazards.

experience.answer: An adult can drop 1–3 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Babies do not give death experience. These are experience points, not player levels.

experience_baby.answer: The baby does not give experience when killed. Growing into an adult changes its death reward; it is separate from experience earned by successful breeding.

experience_breeding.answer: Successful breeding gives 1–7 experience points. That reward comes from breeding, not from killing the baby. The animal’s own breeding requirements still apply.

breeding_age.answer: No. A baby cannot breed; it must grow into an adult first. Food that helps it grow is not the same as breeding food being used on an adult.

growth.answer: A baby chicken normally takes about 20 minutes of active game time to become an adult. You can speed this up by feeding it suitable seeds such as wheat seeds.

diet.answer: Chickens accept suitable seeds, including wheat seeds, beetroot seeds, melon seeds, pumpkin seeds, torchflower seeds and pitcher pods. Feed adults to breed them or chicks to help them grow. Wheat itself is not the same item as wheat seeds.

lifetime.answer: A naturally spawned chicken can disappear through ordinary distance despawning unless it has become persistent. In Bedrock, a name tag is one way to prevent ordinary distance despawning; distance rules depend on simulation settings and mob state. Suitable player interactions, such as breeding, tempting with accepted food or leashing where supported, can also give persistence. A boat or minecart alone is not a blanket persistence guarantee, and persistence does not prevent death.

relocation.answer: You can use a lead to move a chicken. Guide it along a safe route, keep it close enough that the lead does not break, and protect it from falls and unsuitable water or heat.

attack_style.answer: Chickens do not attack players. A chicken jockey is dangerous because of its separate undead rider.

provocation.answer: Hitting an ordinary chicken makes it flee, not retaliate. A rider on it does not change the chicken into the source of the rider’s attacks.

counterplay.answer: If facing a chicken jockey, deal with the rider. For ordinary chickens, use seeds and an enclosure rather than fighting to move them.

identity.answer: A chicken is a passive farm animal that lays eggs. Raise chickens for eggs, feathers, and food, and breed compatible adults using seeds.

behavior.answer: A chicken is a passive farm animal that lays eggs. Raise chickens for eggs, feathers, and food, and breed compatible adults using seeds.

combat.answer: It does not normally attack players. Raise chickens for eggs, feathers, and food, and breed compatible adults using seeds.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 4 health points (2 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

fall_damage.answer: It does not take ordinary fall damage. Other damage sources can still hurt it.

identity.answer: This is the temperate chicken variant.

spawning.answer: Look for temperate chickens in plains, sunflower plains, forest, flower forest, birch forest, old growth birch forest, dark forest, swamp. Those are natural-spawning habitats; a spawn egg can choose this form in additional biomes without making those natural spawning sites.

variants.answer: Breeding inherits a parent’s variant; transporting an adult to another climate does not change its form.

identity.answer: This is the warm chicken variant.

spawning.answer: Look for warm chickens in savanna, savanna plateau, windswept savanna, jungle, sparse jungle, bamboo jungle, badlands, eroded badlands, wooded badlands. Those are natural-spawning habitats; a spawn egg can choose this form in additional biomes without making those natural spawning sites.

variants.answer: Breeding inherits a parent’s variant; transporting an adult to another climate does not change its form.

identity.answer: This is the cold chicken variant.

spawning.answer: Look for cold chickens in taiga, snowy taiga, old growth pine taiga, old growth spruce taiga, windswept hills, windswept gravelly hills, windswept forest, dappled forest. Those are natural-spawning habitats; a spawn egg can choose this form in additional biomes without making those natural spawning sites.

variants.answer: Breeding inherits a parent’s variant; transporting an adult to another climate does not change its form.

spawning.answer: Cod swim in many ocean types, including cold, ordinary and lukewarm oceans and their deep variants. Bedrock also allows them in frozen-ocean variants.

drops.answer: Cod drop raw cod, or cooked cod when killed while burning. In Bedrock a cod can also drop bones.

breeding.answer: Cod cannot be bred with food.

taming.answer: Cod cannot be tamed. Collect one with a water bucket to keep or transport it.

sunlight.answer: Sunlight alone does not make it burn like an exposed zombie or skeleton. Other hazards, such as being out of water or changing dimensions, can still matter for the species.

variants.answer: Cod are a different fish species from salmon, tropical fish and pufferfish. Salmon size variants do not describe cod.

spawn_conditions.answer: Bedrock cod use surface water in normal, cold, frozen and lukewarm oceans and their deep variants, around 12–32 blocks from the player. A roof or spawnable layer above can block the surface spawning check; a river is not their ordinary natural habitat.

leashing.answer: No, you cannot attach an ordinary lead to it through normal player interaction.

bucketing.answer: Use a water bucket directly on the creature to capture it, then use the filled bucket to release it into suitable water. Capturing and releasing it prevents ordinary natural despawning. A dispenser can release a bucketed creature but does not capture one with a water bucket.

experience.answer: It drops 1–3 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. These are experience points, not player levels.

lifetime.answer: Catching it in a water bucket and releasing it prevents ordinary natural despawning. That does not prevent damage or death. A tadpole can still grow into a frog; capture is not a command to stop aging.

relocation.answer: Capture it with a water bucket, carry the filled bucket, and release it into safe water at the destination. Protect aquatic creatures from dry land. A dispenser can release a filled bucket but cannot catch a creature with a water bucket.

growth.answer: A cod has no normal baby form that grows into an adult. There is no ordinary baby-growth timer or growth food to use for this mob.

attack_style.answer: Cod do not attack players or bite for damage. They are passive fish.

provocation.answer: Disturbing cod does not turn them hostile; they try to move away. Do not confuse cod with a defensive pufferfish.

counterplay.answer: Use a water bucket if you want to collect one alive. Keep it in suitable water; fighting is not needed to relocate it.

identity.answer: A cod is a small aquatic fish. Catch it for food or collect the live fish in a water bucket for transport.

behavior.answer: A cod is a small aquatic fish. Catch it for food or collect the live fish in a water bucket for transport.

combat.answer: It does not normally attack players. Catch it for food or collect the live fish in a water bucket for transport.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 3 health points (1.5 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

water.answer: It can breathe underwater. It cannot breathe air normally, so keep it in water.

land.answer: It needs water to breathe normally. Keeping it out of water can cause suffocation damage.

spawning.answer: Command-block minecarts require commands; they have no Survival crafting recipe and do not appear in the normal Bedrock Creative inventory.

interactions.answer: A powered activator rail makes a command-block minecart execute its configured command. This is an operator tool, not ordinary Survival transport.

drops.answer: Breaking one drops a minecart, not a recoverable command block.

storage.answer: It executes commands rather than providing ordinary chest storage or a normal passenger seat.

propulsion.answer: An active activator rail triggers its configured command. It is a command/creator tool, not an ordinary Survival crafting upgrade.

retrieval.answer: Use it only where command permissions allow it. Do not expect an ordinary Survival recipe or a chest interface.

identity.answer: A command block minecart is a rail vehicle that can run commands. Use it in mapmaking systems with the appropriate permissions and powered activator-rail setup.

behavior.answer: A command block minecart is a rail vehicle that can run commands. Use it in mapmaking systems with the appropriate permissions and powered activator-rail setup.

spawning.answer: Copper golems are created by players rather than ordinary animal spawning. A suitable copper golem statue can also be restored to an active golem.

construction.answer: Place a carved pumpkin or jack o’lantern on a copper block to create a copper golem. Use the matching construction supported by your game version.

drops.answer: A copper golem can drop 1–3 copper ingots. Looting does not increase this copper-ingot drop.

interactions.answer: Copper golems move items from copper chests to suitable nearby wooden or trapped chests. Unwaxed golems oxidize over time and can become statues; honeycomb waxes them and an axe can remove wax or oxidation.

taming.answer: Copper golem cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: You cannot breed a copper golem. They are created using their construction or summoning method instead.

oxidation.answer: Unwaxed copper golems oxidize and can become statues. Honeycomb waxes them, and an axe can remove wax or oxidation under the appropriate interaction.
