sunlight.answer: Sunlight alone does not make it burn like an exposed zombie or skeleton. Other hazards, such as being out of water or changing dimensions, can still matter for the species.

fire.answer: Without protection, ordinary fire and lava can damage it. Being undead, large, or adapted to a particular biome does not by itself grant fire immunity.

age_lock.answer: Use a golden dandelion on an eligible baby to pause its aging. Use another golden dandelion on that same baby to resume aging. This is separate from feeding normal food to speed growth.

variants.answer: Glow squid have baby and adult stages. They are a different species from ordinary squid and cannot be bred with food.

spawn_conditions.answer: Check light level 0, Y=-64 through 30, water and a solid roof so the location counts as underground. Ordinary surface squid use a different spawning route. Deep dark is excluded.

leashing.answer: Yes. Use a lead on it to move it, then use a fence to tie it there. You can remove the lead with shears. Leashing does not tame the creature or give it immunity to hazards.

experience.answer: An adult gives 1–3 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Baby squid give no death experience.

experience_baby.answer: Baby squid give no experience when killed.

growth.answer: A baby glow squid normally takes about 20 minutes of active game time to become an adult. Feeding does not speed up its growth. Keep it in water while you wait.

lifetime.answer: A naturally spawned glow squid can disappear through ordinary distance despawning unless it has become persistent. In Bedrock, a name tag is one way to prevent ordinary distance despawning; distance rules depend on simulation settings and mob state. A boat or minecart alone is not a blanket persistence guarantee, and persistence does not prevent death.

relocation.answer: You can use a lead to move a glow squid. Guide it along a safe route, keep it close enough that the lead does not break, and protect it from falls and unsuitable water or heat. Keep it in water: it cannot survive an ordinary dry-land walk.

attack_style.answer: Glow squid do not attack players or shoot damaging ink projectiles. Their luminous appearance is not an attack.

provocation.answer: A glow squid remains passive when disturbed. Its visual glow and ink response are not evidence that it has become hostile.

counterplay.answer: Keep it in water if you are preserving it. It does not light the surrounding blocks like a torch or protect you from monsters.

identity.answer: A glow squid is a passive aquatic animal with a glowing-looking body. It drops glow ink sacs used to brighten signs and make glow item frames. It does not illuminate nearby blocks like a torch.

behavior.answer: A glow squid is a passive aquatic animal with a glowing-looking body. It drops glow ink sacs used to brighten signs and make glow item frames. It does not illuminate nearby blocks like a torch.

combat.answer: It does not normally attack players. It drops glow ink sacs used to brighten signs and make glow item frames. It does not illuminate nearby blocks like a torch.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 10 health points (5 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

water.answer: It can breathe underwater. It cannot breathe air normally, so keep it in water.

land.answer: It needs water to breathe normally. Keeping it out of water can cause suffocation damage.

spawning.answer: Look on snowy slopes, jagged peaks and frozen peaks, on surfaces such as stone, gravel, packed ice and snow blocks.

drops.answer: Goats do not have a normal meat or horn death drop. A goat drops a horn when it rams a suitable solid block, not simply when killed.

breeding.answer: Feed wheat to two adult goats. There is also a rare screaming or screamer variant, and breeding can pass that trait on.

variants.answer: Goats can be ordinary or screamer goats. Screamers look the same but sound different and ram more often; a natural or ordinary-parent breeding outcome has a 2% screamer chance.

interactions.answer: A goat can lose a horn by ramming a suitable block. Avoid killing it if you want horns. An empty bucket can collect milk from an adult goat.

taming.answer: Goat cannot be tamed as player-owned pets. You can still ask how to breed them.

fire.answer: Without protection, it can take fire and lava damage and die. Living in a warm biome or having a particular coat color does not grant fire immunity.

sunlight.answer: Ordinary sunlight does not make this creature spontaneously burn. Fire, lava and lightning are separate hazards.

water.answer: It needs air and can drown if trapped fully underwater. Being able to swim or float is not the same as being able to breathe underwater.

powder_snow.answer: It can take freezing damage while trapped in powder snow without applicable protection. A cold-biome home or white coat alone does not guarantee freezing immunity.

milking.answer: Use an empty bucket on a living adult goat to get milk. Milking does not collect a goat horn.

horns.answer: An adult goat with horns can lose one by ramming stone, coal ore, copper ore, iron ore, emerald ore, logs or packed ice. Killing it is not the horn-harvesting method. A hornless goat cannot supply another horn by being killed.

land.answer: It can live on land. Still provide suitable safe terrain and protect it from fire, falls or other species-specific hazards.

age_lock.answer: Use a golden dandelion on an eligible baby to pause its aging. Use another golden dandelion on that same baby to resume aging. This is separate from feeding normal food to speed growth.

spawn_conditions.answer: Use the correct mountain biome and a suitable surface. Natural spawning after world generation is less common than the original groups. A snowy mountain-looking build in a different biome does not create the required habitat.

leashing.answer: Yes. Use a lead on it to move it, then use a fence to tie it there. You can remove the lead with shears. Leashing does not tame the creature or give it immunity to hazards.

experience.answer: An adult can drop 1–3 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Babies do not give death experience. These are experience points, not player levels.

experience_baby.answer: The baby does not give experience when killed. Growing into an adult changes its death reward; it is separate from experience earned by successful breeding.

experience_breeding.answer: Successful breeding gives 1–7 experience points. That reward comes from breeding, not from killing the baby. The animal’s own breeding requirements still apply.

attack_style.answer: A goat can lower its head and ram an unmoving target, causing knockback that is especially dangerous near cliffs.

provocation.answer: Goats can ram without being hit first. Punching a goat does not trigger ordinary retaliatory attacks; a screamer goat attempts rams more often.

counterplay.answer: Move aside when it lowers its head, and leave room between yourself and cliff edges. Do not stand still expecting a neutral goat to remain harmless.

breeding_age.answer: No. A baby cannot breed; it must grow into an adult first. Food that helps it grow is not the same as breeding food being used on an adult.

growth.answer: A baby goat normally takes about 20 minutes of active game time to become an adult. You can speed this up by feeding it wheat.

diet.answer: Feed wheat to adult goats for breeding or to baby goats to help them grow. This does not tame a goat or stop its occasional ramming behavior.

lifetime.answer: A naturally spawned goat can disappear through ordinary distance despawning unless it has become persistent. In Bedrock, a name tag is one way to prevent ordinary distance despawning; distance rules depend on simulation settings and mob state. Suitable player interactions, such as breeding, tempting with accepted food or leashing where supported, can also give persistence. A boat or minecart alone is not a blanket persistence guarantee, and persistence does not prevent death.

relocation.answer: You can use a lead to move a goat. Guide it along a safe route, keep it close enough that the lead does not break, and protect it from falls and unsuitable water or heat.

identity.answer: A goat is a mountain animal that jumps and sometimes rams entities. Give it space near cliffs. Certain ramming interactions can produce goat horns.

behavior.answer: A goat is a mountain animal that jumps and sometimes rams entities. Give it space near cliffs. Certain ramming interactions can produce goat horns.

combat.answer: It can attack under particular conditions, so do not assume it is always harmless. Give it space near cliffs. Certain ramming interactions can produce goat horns.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 10 health points (5 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

identity.answer: A screamer goat looks like an ordinary goat but makes different sounds and rams more often.

spawning.answer: Look among goats in snowy slopes, jagged peaks and frozen peaks, or breed goats. Screamers are a rare form, not a separate biome population.

horns.answer: Screamer goats can provide the special goat-horn sound group when they ram eligible blocks and still have a horn. Killing a goat is not the horn-harvesting method.

spawning.answer: Look in water at an ocean monument. Bedrock guardian farms use fixed spawning columns tied to the monument.

drops.answer: Guardians can drop prismarine shards, prismarine crystals or cod under their loot conditions. The possible outcomes depend on the kill and loot conditions.

combat.answer: Guardians charge a damaging beam and can hurt attackers with their spikes. Break line of sight to interrupt the beam and use good underwater equipment.

taming.answer: Guardian cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: You cannot breed a guardian.

sunlight.answer: Sunlight alone does not make it burn like an exposed zombie or skeleton. Other hazards, such as being out of water or changing dimensions, can still matter for the species.

fire.answer: Without protection, ordinary fire and lava can damage it. Being undead, large, or adapted to a particular biome does not by itself grant fire immunity.

variants.answer: Guardians and elder guardians are separate mobs; an ordinary guardian does not age into an elder guardian.

spawn_conditions.answer: Bedrock guardians use 25 predetermined columns with water-source checks. Removing the monument blocks alone does not remove those spawning positions. Check the column, water and obstructions.

experience.answer: It gives 10 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Looting affects certain item drops, not this experience reward.

attack_style.answer: A guardian charges a beam attack and has a defensive spike response to melee hits while its spikes are extended.

provocation.answer: Guardians attack players and certain aquatic mobs. Hitting one at close range can hurt you through its defensive spikes, even while you are trying to attack it.

counterplay.answer: Break line of sight with solid cover before the beam finishes charging. Prepare air or Water Breathing and do not treat a shield as complete immunity to its beam or spikes.

growth.answer: A guardian has no normal baby form that grows into an adult. There is no ordinary baby-growth timer or growth food to use for this mob.

lifetime.answer: A naturally spawned guardian can disappear through ordinary distance despawning unless it has become persistent. In Bedrock, a name tag is one way to prevent ordinary distance despawning; distance rules depend on simulation settings and mob state. A boat or minecart alone is not a blanket persistence guarantee, and persistence does not prevent death.

relocation.answer: A minecart can carry a guardian in Bedrock. Bring an empty cart into contact with it, then use rails and powered rails along a protected route. An active activator rail can eject the passenger. This aquatic mob needs a route that does not leave it exposed to unsuitable conditions; it can still attack from the cart. The cart alone does not guarantee persistence in Bedrock.

identity.answer: A guardian is a hostile aquatic mob associated with ocean monuments. It attacks with a damaging beam and can hurt attackers with its defensive spikes.

behavior.answer: A guardian is a hostile aquatic mob associated with ocean monuments. It attacks with a damaging beam and can hurt attackers with its defensive spikes.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 30 health points (15 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

water.answer: It can breathe underwater.

spawning.answer: Waterlog a dried ghast for about 20 minutes to obtain a ghastling, then let it grow into a happy ghast.

drops.answer: A happy ghast drops its equipped harness if it has one. Adult player or tamed-wolf kills can give experience; ghastlings do not give experience.

breeding.answer: Happy ghasts cannot be bred. Make more by rehydrating more dried ghasts.

taming.answer: Happy ghasts do not need wolf-style taming. Grow a ghastling, then equip a harness on the adult.

transport.answer: A harnessed adult happy ghast can carry up to four players. The controlling rider steers it; a ghastling cannot be harnessed or ridden.

interactions.answer: Snowballs accelerate a ghastling’s growth. Use shears to remove an adult’s harness when the interaction is available.

fire.answer: Without protection, it can take fire and lava damage and die. Living in a warm biome or having a particular coat color does not grant fire immunity.

sunlight.answer: Ordinary sunlight does not make this creature spontaneously burn. Fire, lava and lightning are separate hazards.

equipment.answer: Equip an adult happy ghast with a harness, not a saddle. It can carry up to four players. A ghastling must grow up before serving as adult transport.

water.answer: A ghastling can breathe underwater, but an adult happy ghast cannot breathe underwater indefinitely. Baby and adult environmental rules differ.

land.answer: It can live on land. Still provide suitable safe terrain and protect it from fire, falls or other species-specific hazards.

age_lock.answer: Use a golden dandelion on an eligible baby to pause its aging. Use another golden dandelion on that same baby to resume aging. This is separate from feeding normal food to speed growth.

variants.answer: A baby happy ghast is called a ghastling. It grows into a happy ghast; the hostile ghast is a separate mob.

spawn_conditions.answer: Happy ghasts do not use ordinary hostile-ghast spawning. Keep a dried ghast waterlogged until it becomes a ghastling. Snowballs speed up the ghastling’s growth, but two happy ghasts do not breed.

leashing.answer: Yes. Use a lead on it to move it, then use a fence to tie it there. You can remove the lead with shears. Leashing does not tame the creature or give it immunity to hazards.

experience.answer: An adult can drop 1–3 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Babies do not give death experience. These are experience points, not player levels.

experience_baby.answer: The baby does not give experience when killed. Growing into an adult changes its death reward; it is separate from experience earned by successful breeding.

equipment_drops.answer: A happy ghast drops its equipped harness when killed, if it had one. An unequipped ghast does not create a harness as a random drop.

relocation.answer: Equip an adult with a harness for flight; up to four players can ride, and the front rider controls it. Leads can also carry supported mobs or boats below it. A ghastling cannot be harnessed and flown yet.

growth.answer: A ghastling normally takes about 20 minutes of active game time to become an adult happy ghast. Hydrating a dried ghast happens before this and has its own timer. You can speed this up by feeding it snowballs. In Bedrock, 10 snowballs can fully grow a newly spawned ghastling. It cannot be harnessed or ridden while still a ghastling.

diet.answer: Feed snowballs to a ghastling to help it become an adult happy ghast. In Bedrock, 10 snowballs can fully grow a newly spawned ghastling. Snowballs also tempt happy ghasts, but happy ghasts do not breed as a pair.

lifetime.answer: Riding or naming your happy ghast gives it persistence in Bedrock. If it goes missing, also check whether it drifted away, was moved or died; ordinary distance despawning is only one possible cause of a missing mob.

attack_style.answer: Happy ghasts do not shoot hostile-ghast fireballs or deliberately attack players. They are friendly flying mounts.

provocation.answer: A happy ghast does not turn into a hostile ghast when approached or ridden. Riders using weapons remain separate attackers.

counterplay.answer: Use a harness to ride an adult and take care with falls when dismounting. Do not treat a happy ghast as a hostile ghast that needs its fireballs reflected.

identity.answer: A happy ghast is a large friendly flying mob that players can ride with a harness. Use it for aerial transport and building work; it can carry multiple players.

behavior.answer: A happy ghast is a large friendly flying mob that players can ride with a harness. Use it for aerial transport and building work; it can carry multiple players.

combat.answer: It does not normally attack players. Use it for aerial transport and building work; it can carry multiple players.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 20 health points (10 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

fall_damage.answer: It does not take ordinary fall damage. Other damage sources can still hurt it.

identity.answer: A ghastling is the baby stage that grows into a happy ghast.

spawning.answer: Waterlog a dried ghast until it becomes a ghastling. Snowballs can help the ghastling grow; it is not an ordinary hostile ghast spawn.

transport.answer: A ghastling is not the adult flying transport. Let it grow before equipping the adult with a harness.

spawning.answer: Find hoglins in crimson forests and certain bastion areas, especially hoglin stables. Crimson-forest hoglins can respawn over time.

drops.answer: Adult hoglins can drop porkchops and leather. Burning changes porkchops to cooked porkchops. Baby hoglins do not give the adult item loot, although they can give experience.

breeding.answer: Feed crimson fungi to two adult hoglins. They cannot breed while fleeing from warped fungi, respawn anchors or Nether portals.

combat.answer: Hoglins attack and knock targets back. Warped fungi can repel them. Even babies can be aggressive.

interactions.answer: Outside the Nether, a hoglin can convert into a zoglin. A zoglin cannot be bred with crimson fungus like a living hoglin.

taming.answer: Hoglin cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

conversion.answer: A hoglin outside the Nether normally becomes a zoglin after about 15 seconds. A name tag does not prevent that dimension-based conversion.

fire.answer: Hoglins are not normally immune to fire or lava, despite living in the Nether.

sunlight.answer: Sunlight alone does not make it burn like an exposed zombie or skeleton. Other hazards, such as being out of water or changing dimensions, can still matter for the species.

age_lock.answer: Use a golden dandelion on an eligible baby to pause its aging. Use another golden dandelion on that same baby to resume aging. This is separate from feeding normal food to speed growth.

variants.answer: Hoglins have baby and adult stages. Zombification produces a zoglin, which is a different mob rather than an ordinary growth stage.

spawn_conditions.answer: Natural hoglins can spawn at any light level in crimson forests. In Bedrock, Nether wart blocks and shroomlights are unsuitable spawning surfaces. Leave adequate space; bastion-generated hoglins are a separate source.

leashing.answer: Yes. Use a lead on it to move it, then use a fence to tie it there. You can remove the lead with shears. Leashing does not tame the creature or give it immunity to hazards.

experience.answer: Both adults and babies give 5 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Do not apply the usual baby-animal zero-experience rule here.

experience_baby.answer: A baby gives 5 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill, just like an adult.

attack_style.answer: An adult hoglin attacks at close range with its tusks. Young hoglins behave differently from adults.

provocation.answer: Hoglins are hostile animals: being breedable does not make them harmless. They can attack without being hit first.

counterplay.answer: Placed warped fungus, active Nether portals and respawn anchors can repel hoglins. A hoglin already attacking may not stop immediately; maintain space rather than relying on a single repellent block.

breeding_age.answer: No. A baby cannot breed; it must grow into an adult first. Food that helps it grow is not the same as breeding food being used on an adult.

growth.answer: A baby hoglin normally takes about 20 minutes of active game time to become an adult. You can speed this up by feeding it crimson fungus.

diet.answer: Crimson fungus is the breeding food for adult hoglins and helps babies grow. Warped fungus is different: hoglins avoid it instead of using it as breeding food. Feeding does not make a hoglin a tame, harmless pet.

lifetime.answer: A naturally spawned hoglin can disappear through ordinary distance despawning unless it has become persistent. In Bedrock, a name tag is one way to prevent ordinary distance despawning; distance rules depend on simulation settings and mob state. Suitable player interactions, such as breeding, tempting with accepted food or leashing where supported, can also give persistence. A boat or minecart alone is not a blanket persistence guarantee, and persistence does not prevent death.

relocation.answer: You can use a lead to move a hoglin. Guide it along a safe route, keep it close enough that the lead does not break, and protect it from falls and unsuitable water or heat. A lead does not make this hostile mob safe to approach.

identity.answer: A hoglin is a hostile Nether animal found in crimson environments. It attacks at close range and can be bred with crimson fungus. Outside the Nether it can transform into a zoglin.

behavior.answer: A hoglin is a hostile Nether animal found in crimson environments. It attacks at close range and can be bred with crimson fungus. Outside the Nether it can transform into a zoglin.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 40 health points (20 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

spawning.answer: Place a crafted hopper minecart on rails.

interactions.answer: A hopper minecart collects items and can pull items from a container above it. An activator rail can disable or enable its collection; it does not work exactly like a stationary hopper.

drops.answer: Breaking a hopper minecart normally drops its item and stored contents.

storage.answer: A hopper minecart has five slots and pulls dropped items or items from a container above. It can collect through a single solid-block layer but does not push into containers.

propulsion.answer: It travels on rails. A powered activator rail disables collection; an unpowered activator rail reenables it. A hopper below can unload the cart.

retrieval.answer: Breaking it releases stored items. A powered rail and an activator rail perform different jobs, so check which rail is disabling collection.

identity.answer: A hopper minecart is a rail vehicle that collects items. Use it to gather dropped items and move them along tracks, often underneath farms. A powered activator rail changes its collection state.

behavior.answer: A hopper minecart is a rail vehicle that collects items. Use it to gather dropped items and move them along tracks, often underneath farms. A powered activator rail changes its collection state.

spawning.answer: Look for horses in plains and savannas, including some village stables and animal pens.

health.answer: A horse’s maximum health can range from 15 to 30 health points. Health, speed and jumping ability vary between individuals.

drops.answer: Adult horses can drop leather plus equipped saddle and horse armor. Foals have no normal item or experience drops.

taming.answer: Repeatedly mount an adult horse until it accepts you and shows hearts. A saddle is needed to control the tamed horse; putting a saddle on another animal does not tame it.

breeding.answer: Feed golden carrots or golden apples to two tamed adult horses. Breeding a horse with a tamed donkey produces a mule, which cannot breed.

transport.answer: A tamed horse can be controlled with a saddle and equipped with horse armor. Horses cannot carry chests; use a donkey or mule for storage.

variants.answer: Horses combine seven coat colors (white, creamy, chestnut, brown, black, gray and dark brown) with five marking patterns, making 35 combinations. Coat color does not specify a separate biome or guarantee speed, jump or health.

fire.answer: Without protection, it can take fire and lava damage and die. Living in a warm biome or having a particular coat color does not grant fire immunity.

sunlight.answer: Ordinary sunlight does not make this creature spontaneously burn. Fire, lava and lightning are separate hazards.

water.answer: It needs air and can drown if trapped fully underwater. Being able to swim or float is not the same as being able to breathe underwater.

powder_snow.answer: It can take freezing damage while trapped in powder snow without applicable protection. A cold-biome home or white coat alone does not guarantee freezing immunity.

equipment.answer: Equip a tamed adult horse with a saddle to control it while riding. Horse armor is a separate equipment slot; a chest cannot turn an ordinary horse into a pack donkey.

land.answer: It can live on land. Still provide suitable safe terrain and protect it from fire, falls or other species-specific hazards.

age_lock.answer: Use a golden dandelion on an eligible baby to pause its aging. Use another golden dandelion on that same baby to resume aging. This is separate from feeding normal food to speed growth.

spawn_conditions.answer: Natural horses occur in plains and savannas, with some also generated in village animal areas. Coats and markings do not each require a different biome. Donkeys, mules and undead horses have different sources.

leashing.answer: Yes. Use a lead on it to move it, then use a fence to tie it there. You can remove the lead with shears. Leashing does not tame the creature or give it immunity to hazards.

experience.answer: An adult can drop 1–3 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Babies do not give death experience. These are experience points, not player levels.

experience_baby.answer: The baby does not give experience when killed. Growing into an adult changes its death reward; it is separate from experience earned by successful breeding.

experience_breeding.answer: Successful breeding gives 1–7 experience points. That reward comes from breeding, not from killing the baby. The animal’s own breeding requirements still apply.

relocation.answer: Tame an adult and equip a saddle for controlled riding, or use a lead. Coat color does not guarantee speed or jump strength. Keep the route safe for both rider and mount.

breeding_age.answer: No. A baby cannot breed; it must grow into an adult first. Food that helps it grow is not the same as breeding food being used on an adult.

breeding_ownership.answer: The parents must be tamed before breeding. Use eligible adult animals and their breeding food; feeding wild animals is not enough to skip taming.

growth.answer: A baby horse normally takes about 20 minutes of active game time to become an adult. You can speed this up by feeding it wheat, sugar, apples, carrots, golden carrots, golden apples, enchanted golden apples or hay bales.

diet.answer: Living horses accept wheat, sugar, apples, carrots, golden carrots, golden apples, enchanted golden apples and hay bales for feeding uses such as growth, healing or temper. Only golden carrots and golden apples, including enchanted ones, breed tamed adults. Feeding does not replace mounting a horse to tame it.

lifetime.answer: A naturally spawned horse can disappear through ordinary distance despawning unless it has become persistent. In Bedrock, a name tag is one way to prevent ordinary distance despawning; distance rules depend on simulation settings and mob state. Suitable player interactions, such as breeding, tempting with accepted food or leashing where supported, can also give persistence. A boat or minecart alone is not a blanket persistence guarantee, and persistence does not prevent death.

attack_style.answer: Horses do not attack players on their own. A mounted hostile rider is a separate attacker.

provocation.answer: An untamed horse can throw a rider off during taming, but this is not an aggressive melee attack. Feeding and taming do not create a guard animal.

counterplay.answer: Use normal taming and saddling interactions. Handle any hostile rider separately and keep the horse out of dangerous terrain.

identity.answer: A horse is a tameable riding animal. Tame it, equip a saddle to control riding, and use it for fast ground travel. Compatible horses can also wear horse armor.

behavior.answer: A horse is a tameable riding animal. Tame it, equip a saddle to control riding, and use it for fast ground travel. Compatible horses can also wear horse armor.

combat.answer: It does not normally attack players. Tame it, equip a saddle to control riding, and use it for fast ground travel. Compatible horses can also wear horse armor.

spawning.answer: Husks are desert zombie variants that normally appear on the surface, and can also come from suitable trial spawners.

drops.answer: Husks can drop rotten flesh, with rare player-kill drops such as iron ingots, carrots or potatoes. Equipment and jockey-related drops have separate conditions.

combat.answer: Husks attack up close and can give Hunger. Unlike ordinary zombies, they do not burn in sunlight.

interactions.answer: A husk kept submerged can become a regular zombie; a regular zombie can then convert into drowned. Riders and mounts are separate entities.

taming.answer: Husk cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: You cannot breed a husk.

sunlight.answer: Husks do not burn in sunlight like ordinary zombies. They can still take other kinds of damage.

conversion.answer: A husk submerged in water can first convert into a normal zombie. Continued submersion can then turn that zombie into a drowned; it does not skip straight from husk to drowned.

fire.answer: Without protection, ordinary fire and lava can damage it. Being undead, large, or adapted to a particular biome does not by itself grant fire immunity.

growth.answer: Baby undead of this kind do not normally grow into adults while they remain undead. A cured baby zombie villager can later grow as a living villager.

variants.answer: Husks can be babies or adults. Water conversion into a zombie is different from a baby simply growing up.

spawn_conditions.answer: Bedrock husks naturally use desert surface spawning, replacing many ordinary zombies. A dark underground desert tunnel is not the same surface route. Monster-spawner or trial-spawner encounters should be treated separately.

experience.answer: The base reward is 5 experience points for an adult or 12 for a baby after an eligible player or tamed-wolf kill. Naturally spawned equipment can add experience; items picked up later are a separate category.

experience_baby.answer: The base baby reward is 12 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Naturally spawned equipment can add more; this is different from ordinary baby animals giving no experience.

equipment_drops.answer: Naturally spawned weapons or armor are not guaranteed drops. Qualifying player or tamed-wolf kills and Looting can matter. Equipment the mob picked up later is a different category; do not assume one chance covers both. Its ordinary body loot is separate.

attack_style.answer: Husks fight at close range like zombies. An unarmed hit can inflict Hunger; a properly blocked hit does not apply it.

provocation.answer: Husks are hostile on sight and threaten players and villagers. They do not need provocation and do not burn in sunlight.

counterplay.answer: Keep distance or block incoming melee hits with a shield. Do not wait for sunrise to remove husks; use a secure barrier and keep them away from villagers.

lifetime.answer: A naturally spawned husk can disappear through ordinary distance despawning unless it has become persistent. In Bedrock, a name tag is one way to prevent ordinary distance despawning; distance rules depend on simulation settings and mob state. A boat or minecart alone is not a blanket persistence guarantee, and persistence does not prevent death.

relocation.answer: A minecart can carry a husk in Bedrock. Bring an empty cart into contact with it, then use rails and powered rails along a protected route. An active activator rail can eject the passenger. It can still be dangerous while riding; a cart is not taming or protection from its attacks. The cart alone does not guarantee persistence in Bedrock.

identity.answer: A husk is a desert zombie variant that does not burn in sunlight. Its attacks can inflict Hunger, so it remains dangerous even in daytime.

behavior.answer: A husk is a desert zombie variant that does not burn in sunlight. Its attacks can inflict Hunger, so it remains dangerous even in daytime.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 20 health points (10 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

water.answer: It can breathe underwater.

spawning.answer: Find iron golems in villages, or construct one. Bedrock village spawning has bed, villager and working requirements. Three frightened villagers alone are not enough.

construction.answer: Build a T shape with four iron blocks and place a carved pumpkin or jack o’lantern on top last, leaving space for the arms and body.

drops.answer: An iron golem drops 3–5 iron ingots and 0–2 poppies. Looting does not increase those amounts.

health.answer: An iron golem has 100 health points (50 hearts) at full health. Cracks indicate damage levels, not separate maximum-health variants.

interactions.answer: Use iron ingots to repair an iron golem. Naturally spawned golems can become hostile if you attack villagers or damage village standing; a player-built golem has different targeting behavior.

taming.answer: Iron golem cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: You cannot breed an iron golem. They are created using their construction or summoning method instead.

combat.answer: Naturally spawned iron golems can attack players when provoked or when village reputation makes the player a target. Player-built golems do not normally attack their creator. They also defend against many hostile mobs.

repair.answer: Use iron ingots to repair an iron golem. Its cracked appearance shows damage; the cracks do not represent separate maximum-health variants.

sunlight.answer: Sunlight alone does not make it burn like an exposed zombie or skeleton. Other hazards, such as being out of water or changing dimensions, can still matter for the species.

fire.answer: Without protection, ordinary fire and lava can damage it. Being undead, large, or adapted to a particular biome does not by itself grant fire immunity.

water.answer: Iron golems do not drown. They sink rather than swim like a player, but can walk along the bottom. Drowning immunity does not make them immune to lava.

fall_damage.answer: Iron golems are immune to ordinary fall damage. They are not immune to every other damage source.

variants.answer: Iron golems show cracks as their health decreases. Cracks show damage, not a different breed; iron ingots can repair them.

spawn_conditions.answer: A Bedrock village needs at least 20 beds and 10 villagers, all villagers linked to beds, and at least 75% of eligible villagers having worked recently. The village center must be in simulation distance, with a valid unobstructed spawning surface nearby. Three frightened villagers alone are not the Bedrock requirements.

leashing.answer: Yes. Use a lead on it to move it, then use a fence to tie it there. You can remove the lead with shears. Leashing does not tame the creature or give it immunity to hazards.

experience.answer: It gives no experience when killed. Item drops and rewards from other interactions are separate.

attack_style.answer: An iron golem hits at close range and can launch its target upward. It fights many hostile mobs but does not normally target creepers.

provocation.answer: A naturally occurring village golem can become hostile after player aggression or poor village popularity. A player-built iron golem does not attack players even if hit.

counterplay.answer: Avoid provoking village golems. Do not assume your ordinary armor makes their melee attacks safe, or that a village golem will handle a creeper for you.

growth.answer: An iron golem has no normal baby form that grows into an adult. There is no ordinary baby-growth timer or growth food to use for this mob.

lifetime.answer: Iron Golems normally have persistence in Bedrock and do not disappear through ordinary distance despawning. They can still be killed or removed by other game rules.

relocation.answer: You can use a lead to move a iron golem. Guide it along a safe route, keep it close enough that the lead does not break, and protect it from falls and unsuitable water or heat.

identity.answer: An iron golem is a strong guardian mob often associated with villages. It attacks many hostile mobs and can protect a settlement. Attacking villagers or golems can make some golems hostile to you.

behavior.answer: An iron golem is a strong guardian mob often associated with villages. It attacks many hostile mobs and can protect a settlement. Attacking villagers or golems can make some golems hostile to you.

spawning.answer: Lightning occurs during thunderstorms. A suitable Channeling trident hit can also produce lightning.

interactions.answer: Lightning can start fires, damage creatures and transform certain mobs: pigs into zombified piglins, villagers into witches, creepers into charged creepers, and red or brown mooshrooms into the other color.

activation.answer: Thunderstorms, lightning rods and Channeling-related conditions can affect lightning strikes. A strike is an event entity, not a creature you breed.

projectile_effects.answer: Lightning can ignite surroundings, hurt entities and trigger transformations such as pig to zombified piglin or villager to witch. Not every struck animal becomes an undead mount.

retrieval.answer: Lightning cannot be picked up in a bucket or collected as an item. Use suitable lightning-rod placement to manage strikes near a build.

identity.answer: A lightning bolt is a weather event that can also be summoned as an entity. It can damage entities, ignite blocks, and transform certain mobs. Lightning rods help direct nearby strikes.

behavior.answer: A lightning bolt is a weather event that can also be summoned as an entity. It can damage entities, ignite blocks, and transform certain mobs. Lightning rods help direct nearby strikes.

spawning.answer: Throw a lingering potion to create its projectile, which makes an area-effect cloud when it breaks.

interactions.answer: Lingering potions leave a temporary cloud that applies the potion’s effect to eligible entities in its area.

projectile_use.answer: Throw it to create an area-effect cloud after impact. The bottle and the resulting cloud are separate entities.

projectile_effects.answer: A lingering cloud applies its potion effect to eligible creatures entering it. The cloud shrinks over time and when it affects targets.

retrieval.answer: The bottle is consumed. You cannot pick the cloud back up as the original potion.

identity.answer: A lingering potion is a throwable potion that leaves an effect cloud. Entities entering the cloud can receive the potion's effect while the cloud lasts.

behavior.answer: A lingering potion is a throwable potion that leaves an effect cloud. Entities entering the cloud can receive the potion's effect while the cloud lasts.

spawning.answer: Look for llamas in windswept hill biomes and savanna plateaus. Bedrock also allows them in ordinary and windswept savannas.

health.answer: A llama can have 15–30 maximum health points. Storage strength and health vary between individuals.

drops.answer: Adult llamas can drop leather, plus attached chest contents and equipped carpet where applicable. Babies do not have the normal adult item drops.

taming.answer: Repeatedly mount an adult llama until it accepts you and displays hearts. A tamed llama is not steered with a saddle like a horse.

breeding.answer: Feed hay bales to two tamed adult llamas. Wheat can feed a llama but is not the breeding item.

transport.answer: Llamas can carry chests with storage determined by their strength. Lead one to form a caravan. A carpet decorates a llama; it is not a steering saddle.

variants.answer: Llamas have white, cream, gray and brown coats. Carpet color, trader decoration and chest storage are separate from the coat.

fire.answer: Without protection, it can take fire and lava damage and die. Living in a warm biome or having a particular coat color does not grant fire immunity.

sunlight.answer: Ordinary sunlight does not make this creature spontaneously burn. Fire, lava and lightning are separate hazards.

water.answer: It needs air and can drown if trapped fully underwater. Being able to swim or float is not the same as being able to breathe underwater.

powder_snow.answer: It can take freezing damage while trapped in powder snow without applicable protection. A cold-biome home or white coat alone does not guarantee freezing immunity.

storage.answer: A chest gives the llama storage based on its strength. Carpets decorate it but do not set its strength; llamas are not steered with a horse saddle.

equipment.answer: Llamas use carpets for decoration and chests for storage. Riding a llama does not make it steer like a saddled horse.

land.answer: It can live on land. Still provide suitable safe terrain and protect it from fire, falls or other species-specific hazards.

age_lock.answer: Use a golden dandelion on an eligible baby to pause its aging. Use another golden dandelion on that same baby to resume aging. This is separate from feeding normal food to speed growth.

spawn_conditions.answer: Natural llamas require grass blocks, light above 7 and eligible hills or savanna habitats. Bedrock includes regular and windswept savannas as well as savanna plateaus. Trader llamas arrive with wandering traders rather than being ordinary wild herds.

leashing.answer: Yes. Use a lead on it to move it, then use a fence to tie it there. You can remove the lead with shears. Leashing does not tame the creature or give it immunity to hazards.

experience.answer: An adult can drop 1–3 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Babies do not give death experience. These are experience points, not player levels.

experience_baby.answer: The baby does not give experience when killed. Growing into an adult changes its death reward; it is separate from experience earned by successful breeding.

experience_breeding.answer: Successful llama breeding can give experience, but I am not sure of the exact amount. This is separate from the adult’s death reward.

equipment_drops.answer: A llama drops its equipped carpet, attached chest and stored contents when killed. These are separate from ordinary leather drops.

attack_style.answer: A llama retaliates with spit when attacked. Its spit can also accidentally hit other nearby creatures.

provocation.answer: Llamas are normally neutral to players, but retaliate if hurt. They can also react to wolves; a tamed wolf is not treated identically to a wild one.

counterplay.answer: Avoid provoking it or standing between fighting llamas. Taming a llama gives transport-related interactions, not a commandable combat pet.

relocation.answer: Use a lead to guide it and its caravan. Taming lets you interact and ride, but does not give direct saddle-style steering. Carpets are decoration, not steering equipment.

breeding_age.answer: No. A baby cannot breed; it must grow into an adult first. Food that helps it grow is not the same as breeding food being used on an adult.

breeding_ownership.answer: The parents must be tamed before breeding. Use eligible adult animals and their breeding food; feeding wild animals is not enough to skip taming.

growth.answer: A baby llama normally takes about 20 minutes of active game time to become an adult. You can speed this up by feeding it wheat or hay bales.

diet.answer: Wheat and hay bales can heal llamas and help babies grow. To breed tamed adult llamas, use hay bales; wheat is not a breeding substitute.

lifetime.answer: A naturally spawned llama can disappear through ordinary distance despawning unless it has become persistent. In Bedrock, a name tag is one way to prevent ordinary distance despawning; distance rules depend on simulation settings and mob state. Suitable player interactions, such as breeding, tempting with accepted food or leashing where supported, can also give persistence. A boat or minecart alone is not a blanket persistence guarantee, and persistence does not prevent death.

identity.answer: A llama is a tameable pack animal. Equip it with a chest for cargo and use a lead to guide a caravan. It can spit at targets when provoked.

behavior.answer: A llama is a tameable pack animal. Equip it with a chest for cargo and use a lead to guide a caravan. It can spit at targets when provoked.

combat.answer: It can attack under particular conditions, so do not assume it is always harmless. Equip it with a chest for cargo and use a lead to guide a caravan. It can spit at targets when provoked.

identity.answer: This is a white llama coat.

spawning.answer: Look for llamas in suitable savanna and windswept-hill biomes. Their coat colors are not separate biome-exclusive species.

storage.answer: A llama’s strength controls its chest storage capacity; its coat color does not determine that strength.

identity.answer: This is a cream llama coat.

spawning.answer: Look for llamas in suitable savanna and windswept-hill biomes. Their coat colors are not separate biome-exclusive species.

storage.answer: A llama’s strength controls its chest storage capacity; its coat color does not determine that strength.

identity.answer: This is a gray llama coat.

spawning.answer: Look for llamas in suitable savanna and windswept-hill biomes. Their coat colors are not separate biome-exclusive species.

storage.answer: A llama’s strength controls its chest storage capacity; its coat color does not determine that strength.

identity.answer: This is a brown llama coat.

spawning.answer: Look for llamas in suitable savanna and windswept-hill biomes. Their coat colors are not separate biome-exclusive species.

storage.answer: A llama’s strength controls its chest storage capacity; its coat color does not determine that strength.

spawning.answer: Llamas and trader llamas spit when attacking or defending themselves.

combat.answer: Llama spit is a ranged attack, not an item you can collect. A provoked llama or a trader llama defending its trader can spit at a target.

projectile_use.answer: A llama launches spit while retaliating against a target. It is a projectile, not an item the player fires from inventory.

projectile_effects.answer: The spit can hurt a target or accidentally hit another creature, potentially starting another fight.

retrieval.answer: The fired spit cannot be picked up and stored as ammunition.

identity.answer: Llama spit is the projectile a llama spits at a target. It is a defensive ranged attack rather than an item you normally collect.

behavior.answer: Llama spit is the projectile a llama spits at a target. It is a defensive ranged attack rather than an item you normally collect.

spawning.answer: Find magma cubes in the Nether, especially basalt deltas, and from magma-cube spawners in bastion treasure rooms.

health.answer: Large magma cubes have 16 health points, medium cubes have 4 and small cubes have 1. Killing a larger cube can split it into smaller cubes.

drops.answer: Medium and large magma cubes can drop magma cream; the small size does not normally drop it. If a frog eats a small magma cube, the result is a froglight whose color depends on the frog.

combat.answer: Magma cubes damage targets on contact and can split into smaller attackers. They are resistant to fire and lava; the smallest size can still hurt you.

taming.answer: Magma cube cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: You cannot breed a magma cube. Larger ones split into smaller ones when killed; that is not food-based breeding.

powder_snow.answer: Magma cubes take extra freezing damage in powder snow even though ordinary fire and lava do not hurt them.

variants.answer: Magma cubes have small, medium and large forms. Larger cubes split into smaller ones when killed; splitting is not food-based breeding.

water.answer: It can swim, but staying submerged for 15 seconds starts drowning damage. A larger cube can split into smaller cubes when it dies. Lava immunity does not mean immunity to drowning.

spawn_conditions.answer: Natural magma-cube spawning permits any light level but needs enough clear space without solid or liquid obstructions. Space is checked before the cube’s final size is selected, so a tiny gap is not sufficient just because small cubes exist. Monster spawners are a separate source.

experience.answer: Small, medium and large cubes give 1, 2 and 4 experience points respectively after a qualifying player kill. Those values are per cube killed, not a combined total for every smaller cube that might split from it.

attack_style.answer: Magma cubes hop into targets and split into smaller cubes when killed. Even the small form can hurt players.

provocation.answer: Magma cubes are hostile and fire-immune. Small magma cubes are not harmless like the smallest ordinary slimes.

counterplay.answer: Use room and cover to handle split offspring, and do not use fire as your main attack. Watch for lava around the fight; killing one large cube may leave several smaller threats.

growth.answer: Small magma cubes are size variants, not growing babies. Waiting or feeding does not grow them into larger cubes; larger magma cubes split into smaller ones when killed.

lifetime.answer: A naturally spawned magma cube can disappear through ordinary distance despawning unless it has become persistent. In Bedrock, a name tag is one way to prevent ordinary distance despawning; distance rules depend on simulation settings and mob state. A boat or minecart alone is not a blanket persistence guarantee, and persistence does not prevent death.

relocation.answer: A minecart can carry a magma cube in Bedrock. Bring an empty cart into contact with it, then use rails and powered rails along a protected route. An active activator rail can eject the passenger. It can still be dangerous while riding; a cart is not taming or protection from its attacks. The cart alone does not guarantee persistence in Bedrock.

identity.answer: A magma cube is a bouncing hostile Nether mob. Larger cubes split into smaller ones when killed. Their drops are used for magma cream and related recipes.

behavior.answer: A magma cube is a bouncing hostile Nether mob. Larger cubes split into smaller ones when killed. Their drops are used for magma cream and related recipes.

fire.answer: It is immune to ordinary fire and lava damage. That does not protect it from every other kind of damage.

sunlight.answer: It is fire-immune, so sunlight does not make it take ordinary burning damage.

fall_damage.answer: It does not take ordinary fall damage. Other damage sources can still hurt it.

identity.answer: This is the small magma cube size.

health.answer: This size has 1 health points.

drops.answer: Medium and large magma cubes can drop magma cream. Small magma cubes do not have the ordinary magma-cream drop; a frog eating a small one makes a froglight.

identity.answer: This is the medium magma cube size.

health.answer: This size has 4 health points.

drops.answer: Medium and large magma cubes can drop magma cream. Small magma cubes do not have the ordinary magma-cream drop; a frog eating a small one makes a froglight.

identity.answer: This is the large magma cube size.

health.answer: This size has 16 health points.

drops.answer: Medium and large magma cubes can drop magma cream. Small magma cubes do not have the ordinary magma-cream drop; a frog eating a small one makes a froglight.

spawning.answer: Place a minecart item on rails.

transport.answer: Minecarts move along rails and can carry a rider. Powered rails provide propulsion when powered; ordinary rails do not supply continuous power.

drops.answer: Breaking a minecart normally drops its minecart item.

storage.answer: A normal minecart carries a passenger rather than a chest inventory. Cargo minecarts are different entities.

propulsion.answer: Place it on rails. Powered rails supply motion, while ordinary rails guide the route; a passenger does not simply paddle it like a boat.

retrieval.answer: Breaking the cart releases its passenger. Hostile passengers do not become harmless merely because they are in a cart.

identity.answer: A minecart is a rail vehicle for transporting entities. Place it on rails and use powered track or other mechanisms to move riders along a route.

behavior.answer: A minecart is a rail vehicle for transporting entities. Place it on rails and use powered track or other mechanisms to move riders along a route.

spawning.answer: Red mooshrooms naturally spawn on mycelium in mushroom fields. Brown mooshrooms come from special transformations or rare breeding outcomes rather than ordinary natural spawning.

drops.answer: Adult mooshrooms have cow-like leather and beef drops. Shearing is different: it gives mushrooms and turns the mooshroom into a cow.

breeding.answer: Feed wheat to two adult mooshrooms. They cannot breed with ordinary cows. Same-color parents have a rare chance to produce the opposite-color variant.

variants.answer: Red mooshrooms spawn naturally in mushroom fields. Brown mooshrooms come from lightning conversion or a rare breeding mutation; a red/brown pair can produce either color.

interactions.answer: Use a bucket for milk or a bowl for mushroom stew. A brown mooshroom fed a suitable flower gives suspicious stew on the next bowl interaction. Shearing permanently converts it into a cow.

taming.answer: Mooshroom cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

fire.answer: Without protection, it can take fire and lava damage and die. Living in a warm biome or having a particular coat color does not grant fire immunity.

sunlight.answer: Ordinary sunlight does not make this creature spontaneously burn. Fire, lava and lightning are separate hazards.

water.answer: It needs air and can drown if trapped fully underwater. Being able to swim or float is not the same as being able to breathe underwater.

powder_snow.answer: It can take freezing damage while trapped in powder snow without applicable protection. A cold-biome home or white coat alone does not guarantee freezing immunity.

lightning.answer: Lightning swaps a mooshroom between red and brown. It does not always turn every struck mooshroom brown; an already-brown one turns red.

shearing.answer: Shearing an adult mooshroom gives five matching mushrooms and converts it into a cow. The mushrooms do not grow back on that cow.

milking.answer: Use a bucket for milk or a bowl for mushroom stew. A brown mooshroom fed a suitable small flower gives the corresponding suspicious stew on the next bowl milking; red mooshrooms do not.

conversion.answer: Shearing turns a mooshroom into a cow. Lightning instead switches its red/brown form. Those two interactions do not have the same result.

land.answer: It can live on land. Still provide suitable safe terrain and protect it from fire, falls or other species-specific hazards.

age_lock.answer: Use a golden dandelion on an eligible baby to pause its aging. Use another golden dandelion on that same baby to resume aging. This is separate from feeding normal food to speed growth.

spawn_conditions.answer: Natural red mooshrooms require mushroom fields and mycelium. Brown mooshrooms do not naturally spawn: use lightning conversion or the rare opposite-color offspring from breeding two matching mooshrooms. Ordinary cows and red mushrooms do not combine into a mooshroom.

leashing.answer: Yes. Use a lead on it to move it, then use a fence to tie it there. You can remove the lead with shears. Leashing does not tame the creature or give it immunity to hazards.

experience.answer: An adult can drop 1–3 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Babies do not give death experience. These are experience points, not player levels.

experience_baby.answer: The baby does not give experience when killed. Growing into an adult changes its death reward; it is separate from experience earned by successful breeding.

experience_breeding.answer: Successful breeding gives 1–7 experience points. That reward comes from breeding, not from killing the baby. The animal’s own breeding requirements still apply.

breeding_age.answer: No. A baby cannot breed; it must grow into an adult first. Food that helps it grow is not the same as breeding food being used on an adult.

growth.answer: A baby mooshroom normally takes about 20 minutes of active game time to become an adult. You can speed this up by feeding it wheat.

diet.answer: Wheat breeds adult mooshrooms and helps babies grow. A brown mooshroom can also accept a suitable small flower to set the effect of its next suspicious stew; that flower interaction is separate from wheat breeding.

lifetime.answer: A naturally spawned mooshroom can disappear through ordinary distance despawning unless it has become persistent. In Bedrock, a name tag is one way to prevent ordinary distance despawning; distance rules depend on simulation settings and mob state. Suitable player interactions, such as breeding, tempting with accepted food or leashing where supported, can also give persistence. A boat or minecart alone is not a blanket persistence guarantee, and persistence does not prevent death.

relocation.answer: You can use a lead to move a mooshroom. Guide it along a safe route, keep it close enough that the lead does not break, and protect it from falls and unsuitable water or heat.

attack_style.answer: Mooshrooms do not attack players. Red and brown variants remain passive.

provocation.answer: Hitting a mooshroom makes it flee rather than fight back. A lightning-based variant change is not a hostile transformation.

counterplay.answer: For mushrooms, consider that shearing permanently changes a mooshroom into a cow. Use buckets or bowls for renewable milk and stew rather than treating it as a hostile enemy.

identity.answer: A mooshroom is a mushroom-covered cow variant. It can be milked and can provide mushroom stew when used with a bowl. Shearing it changes it into an ordinary cow.

behavior.answer: A mooshroom is a mushroom-covered cow variant. It can be milked and can provide mushroom stew when used with a bowl. Shearing it changes it into an ordinary cow.

combat.answer: It does not normally attack players. It can be milked and can provide mushroom stew when used with a bowl. Shearing it changes it into an ordinary cow.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 10 health points (5 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

identity.answer: This is a red mooshroom.

spawning.answer: Find red mooshrooms in mushroom fields.

milking.answer: Use a bucket for milk or a bowl for mushroom stew. Red mooshrooms do not make suspicious stew from flowers.

lightning.answer: A lightning strike changes red and brown mooshrooms into the other color.

identity.answer: This is a brown mooshroom.

spawning.answer: Red mooshrooms naturally spawn in mushroom fields. Lightning changes red to brown and brown to red; breeding two red parents also has a rare brown mutation.

milking.answer: A brown mooshroom can make suspicious stew after being fed a suitable small flower; use a bowl. It returns to ordinary mushroom stew until fed another flower.

lightning.answer: A lightning strike changes red and brown mooshrooms into the other color.

flower_effects.scope: Effects only, no unreviewed duration or future-effect claims.

spawning.answer: Obtain a mule by breeding a horse with a donkey. Mules do not naturally spawn in a biome.

health.answer: A mule’s maximum health can range from 15 to 30 health points.

drops.answer: Adult mules can drop leather, plus an equipped saddle, attached chest and stored contents. Babies have no normal item or experience drops.

taming.answer: Repeatedly mount an adult mule until it accepts you and shows hearts. Equip a saddle to control it.

breeding.answer: Mules cannot breed. Produce another mule by breeding a tamed horse and a tamed donkey with golden carrots or golden apples.

transport.answer: A tamed, saddled mule can carry a chest. It cannot wear horse armor.

fire.answer: Without protection, it can take fire and lava damage and die. Living in a warm biome or having a particular coat color does not grant fire immunity.

sunlight.answer: Ordinary sunlight does not make this creature spontaneously burn. Fire, lava and lightning are separate hazards.

water.answer: It needs air and can drown if trapped fully underwater. Being able to swim or float is not the same as being able to breathe underwater.

powder_snow.answer: It can take freezing damage while trapped in powder snow without applicable protection. A cold-biome home or white coat alone does not guarantee freezing immunity.

storage.answer: A tamed donkey or mule can be equipped with a chest to carry inventory. Its storage chest and riding saddle are separate pieces of equipment.

equipment.answer: Use a saddle on the tamed animal to control riding, and optionally a chest for storage. It does not use ordinary horse armor.

land.answer: It can live on land. Still provide suitable safe terrain and protect it from fire, falls or other species-specific hazards.

age_lock.answer: Use a golden dandelion on an eligible baby to pause its aging. Use another golden dandelion on that same baby to resume aging. This is separate from feeding normal food to speed growth.

variants.answer: Mules have baby and adult stages. They come from breeding a horse with a donkey and cannot breed themselves.

spawn_conditions.answer: Breed a horse and donkey rather than waiting for a wild mule. Mules cannot breed with each other.

leashing.answer: Yes. Use a lead on it to move it, then use a fence to tie it there. You can remove the lead with shears. Leashing does not tame the creature or give it immunity to hazards.

experience.answer: An adult can drop 1–3 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Babies do not give death experience. These are experience points, not player levels.

experience_baby.answer: The baby does not give experience when killed. Growing into an adult changes its death reward; it is separate from experience earned by successful breeding.

equipment_drops.answer: An equipped mule drops its saddle, attached chest and stored contents when killed. It does not create a second copy of those items.

relocation.answer: Tame and saddle it for controlled riding, or use a lead. Its attached chest and contents travel with it, but carrying cargo does not protect it from hazards.

growth.answer: A baby mule normally takes about 20 minutes of active game time to become an adult. You can speed this up by feeding it wheat, sugar, apples, carrots, golden carrots, golden apples, enchanted golden apples or hay bales. A mule can grow up even though adult mules cannot breed.

diet.answer: Mules accept wheat, sugar, apples, carrots, golden carrots, golden apples, enchanted golden apples and hay bales for growth or adult healing. A mule cannot breed even if it accepts a golden carrot or golden apple.

lifetime.answer: A naturally spawned mule can disappear through ordinary distance despawning unless it has become persistent. In Bedrock, a name tag is one way to prevent ordinary distance despawning; distance rules depend on simulation settings and mob state. Suitable player interactions, such as breeding, tempting with accepted food or leashing where supported, can also give persistence. A boat or minecart alone is not a blanket persistence guarantee, and persistence does not prevent death.

attack_style.answer: Mules do not attack players. They are passive pack mounts rather than combat pets.

provocation.answer: Bucking during taming does not make a mule a hostile mob. Feeding a mule does not enable breeding or attack commands.

counterplay.answer: Tame and saddle the mule for riding, or equip a chest for transport. Protect it from hazards rather than expecting it to defend you.

identity.answer: A mule is a rideable pack animal produced by breeding a horse and donkey. Tame and saddle it for travel, or add a chest for supplies. Mules cannot breed.

behavior.answer: A mule is a rideable pack animal produced by breeding a horse and donkey. Tame and saddle it for travel, or add a chest for supplies. Mules cannot breed.

combat.answer: It does not normally attack players. Tame and saddle it for travel, or add a chest for supplies. Mules cannot breed.

spawning.answer: Look in ocean biomes between Y=38 and Y=58, usually in small groups.

drops.answer: A nautilus can rarely drop a nautilus shell under the appropriate player or tamed-wolf kill conditions. Equipped saddle and nautilus armor also drop.

taming.answer: Feed pufferfish or a bucket of pufferfish to a nautilus. Each feeding may tame it, so bring more than one.

breeding.answer: At full health, suitable adult nautiluses can breed when fed fish or buckets of fish. Feeding a hurt one heals it first.

transport.answer: Equip a tamed adult nautilus with a saddle to ride it underwater. Nautilus armor provides additional protection; a ridden nautilus has its own underwater-breathing interaction.

combat.answer: Untamed adult nautiluses can retaliate with a dash when provoked and attack pufferfish. Tamed and baby nautiluses are normally passive. Stay clear of the dash path even if another creature is the target.

equipment.answer: A tamed adult uses a saddle for riding and can wear nautilus armor. Treat its rider and mount as separate entities if it originally spawned with a drowned.

sunlight.answer: Sunlight alone does not make it burn like an exposed zombie or skeleton. Other hazards, such as being out of water or changing dimensions, can still matter for the species.

fire.answer: Without protection, ordinary fire and lava can damage it. Being undead, large, or adapted to a particular biome does not by itself grant fire immunity.

age_lock.answer: Use a golden dandelion on an eligible baby to pause its aging. Use another golden dandelion on that same baby to resume aging. This is separate from feeding normal food to speed growth.

variants.answer: Nautiluses have baby and adult stages and can be wild or tamed. A zombie nautilus is a separate undead mob.

spawn_conditions.answer: Natural nautiluses need ocean water in the Y=38–58 range. A shallow river is not their natural habitat. Zombie nautiluses use a separate drowned-jockey route.

leashing.answer: You can attach a lead while it is not angry. If it becomes angry while already leashed, that alone does not break the lead, but you cannot reattach one while it remains angry. Leashing does not tame it.

experience.answer: An adult can drop 1–3 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Babies do not give death experience. These are experience points, not player levels.

experience_baby.answer: The baby does not give experience when killed. Growing into an adult changes its death reward; it is separate from experience earned by successful breeding.

equipment_drops.answer: A nautilus drops its equipped saddle and nautilus armor when killed, if it had them. It does not generate armor merely because you used Looting.

lifetime.answer: Wild nautiluses can despawn. A player interaction makes a nautilus persistent; taming and riding are separate interactions. Persistence does not stop it suffocating on land or dying from damage.

relocation.answer: Tame it and equip a saddle for controlled underwater riding, or use a lead while it is calm. Keep it in water; it can suffocate on land. Your rider breathing protection does not mean the mount is safe everywhere.

breeding_age.answer: No. A baby cannot breed; it must grow into an adult first. Food that helps it grow is not the same as breeding food being used on an adult.

growth.answer: A baby nautilus normally takes about 20 minutes of active game time to become an adult. You can speed this up by feeding it fish or buckets of fish. In Bedrock, 10 suitable fish or buckets of fish can fully grow a newly spawned baby nautilus.

diet.answer: Nautiluses accept fish and buckets of fish for healing, growth and breeding. Taming specifically needs pufferfish or a bucket of pufferfish. Cod, salmon or tropical fish can have feeding uses without being taming food.

attack_style.answer: An untamed adult nautilus can retaliate with a damaging dash and attacks pufferfish. Tamed and baby nautiluses are normally passive.

provocation.answer: Attacking a wild adult nautilus can provoke it. A tamed nautilus and a harmless baby do not have the same retaliation state as an angry wild adult.

counterplay.answer: Avoid provoking a wild adult and stay out of its dash path. Tame with pufferfish when safe; another fish being accepted for healing does not mean it tames the nautilus.

identity.answer: A nautilus is an aquatic animal that can become a rideable mount. Tame and equip a suitable adult to travel underwater; keep it in appropriate water conditions.

behavior.answer: A nautilus is an aquatic animal that can become a rideable mount. Tame and equip a suitable adult to travel underwater; keep it in appropriate water conditions.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 15 health points (7.5 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

water.answer: It can breathe underwater. It cannot breathe air normally, so keep it in water.

land.answer: It needs water to breathe normally. Keeping it out of water can cause suffocation damage.

spawning.answer: NPCs are creator-controlled characters obtained through supported commands or world-authoring features, not normal natural mob spawning.

interactions.answer: Creator settings define an NPC’s dialogue and actions. Interacting with it is not a way to tame it or change its profession with a workstation.

availability.answer: NPCs are creator/Education-oriented characters that use configured dialogue and commands. They are not villagers that breed and trade through ordinary Survival rules.

identity.answer: An NPC is a special character entity used in compatible Education and mapmaking worlds. Creators can configure dialogue and actions; it is not an ordinary naturally spawning Survival villager.

behavior.answer: An NPC is a special character entity used in compatible Education and mapmaking worlds. Creators can configure dialogue and actions; it is not an ordinary naturally spawning Survival villager.

fire.answer: It is immune to ordinary fire and lava damage. That does not protect it from every other kind of damage.

sunlight.answer: Ordinary sunlight does not make it take burning damage. It is fire-immune, although other environmental hazards can still matter.

spawning.answer: Look in jungles, bamboo jungles and sparse jungles in Bedrock, on grass blocks.

drops.answer: Ocelots have no normal item drop. Adults can give experience when killed by a player or tamed wolf.

breeding.answer: Feed raw cod or raw salmon to two trusting adult ocelots. In Bedrock the baby trusts the player.

taming.answer: Ocelots gain trust from raw cod or raw salmon, but no longer turn into pet cats. Trust is not the same as owning a tamed cat.

interactions.answer: Approach slowly with raw fish. A trusting ocelot stops fleeing from you, and ocelots help scare creepers.

health.answer: Ocelots have 10 health points (5 hearts). Trusting an ocelot does not turn it into a tamed cat or give it a separate tamed-cat health value.

fire.answer: Without protection, it can take fire and lava damage and die. Living in a warm biome or having a particular coat color does not grant fire immunity.

sunlight.answer: Ordinary sunlight does not make this creature spontaneously burn. Fire, lava and lightning are separate hazards.

water.answer: It needs air and can drown if trapped fully underwater. Being able to swim or float is not the same as being able to breathe underwater.

powder_snow.answer: It can take freezing damage while trapped in powder snow without applicable protection. A cold-biome home or white coat alone does not guarantee freezing immunity.

land.answer: It can live on land. Still provide suitable safe terrain and protect it from fire, falls or other species-specific hazards.

age_lock.answer: Use a golden dandelion on an eligible baby to pause its aging. Use another golden dandelion on that same baby to resume aging. This is separate from feeding normal food to speed growth.

variants.answer: Baby and adult ocelots can become trusting, but a trusting ocelot does not turn into a pet cat. Cats are a separate mob.

spawn_conditions.answer: Bedrock ocelots can naturally spawn in all jungle types at light level 7 or above. Grass blocks matter. Sparse jungle is an eligible habitat.

leashing.answer: Yes. Use a lead on it to move it, then use a fence to tie it there. You can remove the lead with shears. Leashing does not tame the creature or give it immunity to hazards.

trust.answer: Approach carefully with raw cod or raw salmon and feed it until hearts appear. A trusting ocelot stops fleeing, but does not turn into a pet cat or gain a wolf-style sit command. In Bedrock, a baby bred from trusting ocelots trusts the player.

experience.answer: An adult can drop 1–3 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Babies do not give death experience. These are experience points, not player levels.

experience_baby.answer: The baby does not give experience when killed. Growing into an adult changes its death reward; it is separate from experience earned by successful breeding.

experience_breeding.answer: Successful breeding gives 1–7 experience points. That reward comes from breeding, not from killing the baby. The animal’s own breeding requirements still apply.

lifetime.answer: A trusting ocelot does not naturally despawn. Gain its trust with raw cod or raw salmon. Trust does not make it a commandable pet cat or keep it safe from attacks.

breeding_age.answer: No. A baby cannot breed; it must grow into an adult first. Food that helps it grow is not the same as breeding food being used on an adult.

growth.answer: A baby ocelot normally takes about 20 minutes of active game time to become an adult. You can speed this up by feeding it raw cod or raw salmon.

diet.answer: Raw cod and raw salmon can gain an ocelot’s trust, breed adults or help kittens grow. A trusting ocelot does not turn into a tamed cat.

relocation.answer: You can use a lead to move a ocelot. Guide it along a safe route, keep it close enough that the lead does not break, and protect it from falls and unsuitable water or heat.

attack_style.answer: Ocelots do not attack players, but hunt prey such as chickens and baby turtles.

provocation.answer: An ocelot normally flees from a nearby player rather than fighting. Gaining its trust does not convert it into a domestic cat or guard pet.

counterplay.answer: Approach carefully with raw cod or salmon to gain trust, and keep vulnerable prey separate. Do not attack it to try to make it follow.

identity.answer: An ocelot is a wild jungle cat. Feeding suitable raw fish can gain its trust, but it does not become a domestic cat. Ocelots help keep creepers away.

behavior.answer: An ocelot is a wild jungle cat. Feeding suitable raw fish can gain its trust, but it does not become a domestic cat. Ocelots help keep creepers away.

combat.answer: It does not normally attack players. Feeding suitable raw fish can gain its trust, but it does not become a domestic cat. Ocelots help keep creepers away.

fall_damage.answer: It does not take ordinary fall damage. Other damage sources can still hurt it.

spawning.answer: Ominous trial spawners create these temporary entities above players or trial mobs during an ominous trial.

interactions.answer: An ominous item spawner displays an item, then releases a projectile or potion. Watch overhead during ominous trials; this is a hazard mechanism, not an ordinary loot chest.

activation.answer: An ominous trial spawner can create this overhead item-spawner entity during an ominous trial. It displays an item briefly before releasing it downward.

projectile_effects.answer: If the displayed item is a projectile it is fired; otherwise it is dropped. Watch the displayed item and overhead hazards rather than assuming every outcome is helpful loot.

retrieval.answer: The item-spawner entity itself is not an ordinary collectible spawner block. A released item and the entity that released it are different things.

identity.answer: An ominous item spawner is a special entity used in ominous-trial encounters. It creates falling items or projectiles as part of trial mechanics, rather than acting as a normal tameable mob.

behavior.answer: An ominous item spawner is a special entity used in ominous-trial encounters. It creates falling items or projectiles as part of trial mechanics, rather than acting as a normal tameable mob.

spawning.answer: Look in jungles, especially bamboo jungles. Pandas naturally appear on grass blocks rather than podzol.

health.answer: Most pandas have 20 health points (10 hearts); weak pandas have 10 health points (5 hearts).

drops.answer: Adult pandas can drop bamboo. Baby pandas can sometimes produce slimeballs when sneezing; that is not a normal death drop.

breeding.answer: Feed bamboo to two adult pandas with at least eight bamboo plants within five blocks of each panda. In Bedrock, too little nearby planted bamboo makes them eat rather than enter love mode.

variants.answer: Panda personalities are normal, lazy, worried, playful, aggressive, weak and brown. Genetics determine the form; weak pandas have reduced health, and brown is a recessive appearance.

interactions.answer: Pandas eat bamboo and cake. Baby pandas can sneeze, sometimes producing slimeballs. Different personalities change behavior; do not treat every panda as the same temperament.

taming.answer: Panda cannot be tamed as player-owned pets. You can still ask how to breed them.

combat.answer: Adult pandas can retaliate when hit, and their personality affects their reactions. Baby pandas are passive; do not assume every adult panda behaves like a passive farm animal.

fire.answer: Without protection, it can take fire and lava damage and die. Living in a warm biome or having a particular coat color does not grant fire immunity.

sunlight.answer: Ordinary sunlight does not make this creature spontaneously burn. Fire, lava and lightning are separate hazards.
