spawning.answer: Look on sandy beaches, excluding snowy beaches and stony shores. In Bedrock, natural turtles spawn at Y=60–67.

drops.answer: Adult turtles can drop seagrass. A lightning kill has a separate bowl-drop rule. Turtle scutes are produced when babies grow into adults, not by killing adults.

breeding.answer: Feed seagrass to two adult turtles. The pregnant turtle returns to its home beach to lay eggs on suitable sand; protect the eggs from trampling and hostile mobs.

interactions.answer: A baby turtle drops a scute when it becomes an adult. Move eggs with Silk Touch if needed; relocated eggs do not keep their previous cracking progress.

taming.answer: Turtle cannot be tamed as player-owned pets. You can still ask how to breed them.

fire.answer: Without protection, it can take fire and lava damage and die. Living in a warm biome or having a particular coat color does not grant fire immunity.

sunlight.answer: Ordinary sunlight does not make this creature spontaneously burn. Fire, lava and lightning are separate hazards.

powder_snow.answer: It can take freezing damage while trapped in powder snow without applicable protection. A cold-biome home or white coat alone does not guarantee freezing immunity.

hatching.answer: Turtle eggs need suitable sand and progress through cracking stages, with much faster hatching at night. Protect them from trampling and hostile mobs. The parents lay eggs at their home beach.

land.answer: It can live on land. Still provide suitable safe terrain and protect it from fire, falls or other species-specific hazards.

age_lock.answer: Use a golden dandelion on an eligible baby to pause its aging. Use another golden dandelion on that same baby to resume aging. This is separate from feeding normal food to speed growth.

variants.answer: Turtles have baby and adult stages. Their home beach is a location they remember, not a different coat variety.

spawn_conditions.answer: Check an eligible beach, sand and Y=60–67 for natural Bedrock turtles. Breeding is different: a turtle returns to its home beach to lay eggs, so a random new sand pen may not be its chosen nesting place.

leashing.answer: No, you cannot attach an ordinary lead to it through normal player interaction.

nesting.answer: A turtle returns to its remembered home beach to lay eggs after breeding with seagrass. Moving an adult to a new pen does not change that home. Move eggs with Silk Touch and hatch them at the new location to establish a new home beach for those babies.

harvesting.answer: A baby turtle drops a turtle scute when it grows into an adult. Killing or shearing an adult turtle is not the turtle-scute method. Armadillo scutes are a different item used for wolf armor.

experience.answer: An adult can drop 1–3 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Babies do not give death experience. These are experience points, not player levels.

experience_baby.answer: The baby does not give experience when killed. Growing into an adult changes its death reward; it is separate from experience earned by successful breeding.

experience_breeding.answer: Successful breeding gives 1–7 experience points. That reward comes from breeding, not from killing the baby. The animal’s own breeding requirements still apply.

relocation.answer: You cannot attach a normal lead. Seagrass can guide it, but a breeding adult may return to its remembered home beach. Moving eggs with Silk Touch and hatching them at a new beach establishes a home there for the new turtles.

breeding_age.answer: No. A baby cannot breed; it must grow into an adult first. Food that helps it grow is not the same as breeding food being used on an adult.

growth.answer: A baby turtle normally takes about 20 minutes of active game time to become an adult. You can speed this up by feeding it seagrass. It drops a turtle scute when it becomes an adult; killing the baby is not how to obtain that scute.

diet.answer: Feed seagrass to adult turtles for breeding or to babies to help them grow. A baby drops a turtle scute when it becomes an adult; you do not get that growth scute by killing it.

lifetime.answer: A naturally spawned turtle can disappear through ordinary distance despawning unless it has become persistent. In Bedrock, a name tag is one way to prevent ordinary distance despawning; distance rules depend on simulation settings and mob state. Suitable player interactions, such as breeding, tempting with accepted food or leashing where supported, can also give persistence. A boat or minecart alone is not a blanket persistence guarantee, and persistence does not prevent death.

attack_style.answer: Turtles do not attack players, even around their eggs. They do not defend nests like an aggressive guard mob.

provocation.answer: A turtle remains passive when disturbed. Eggs and babies can still attract threats, but those threats are other mobs.

counterplay.answer: Protect eggs and babies from predators and trampling. Use seagrass for breeding or baby growth rather than fighting the adults.

identity.answer: A turtle is a passive coastal animal. Breed it with seagrass to produce eggs on its home beach. Babies shed turtle scutes when they grow up.

behavior.answer: A turtle is a passive coastal animal. Breed it with seagrass to produce eggs on its home beach. Babies shed turtle scutes when they grow up.

combat.answer: It does not normally attack players. Breed it with seagrass to produce eggs on its home beach. Babies shed turtle scutes when they grow up.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 30 health points (15 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

water.answer: It can breathe underwater. It can also breathe air.

health.answer: Vexes have 14 health points (7 hearts).

spawning.answer: Evokers summon vexes during combat. They do not normally spawn throughout the landscape.

drops.answer: Vexes do not drop their iron swords, even with Looting. A player or tamed-wolf kill can give experience.

combat.answer: Vexes fly through blocks and attack with swords. Walls alone will not stop them; deal with the evoker that summons them.

taming.answer: Vex cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: You cannot breed a vex.

variants.answer: Vexes glow red while attacking. This is an attack state, not a separate red species. Evoker-summoned vexes also have a limited lifetime.

lifetime.answer: An evoker-summoned vex starts taking lifetime damage after 30 to 119 seconds and eventually dies, even in a boat or minecart. This is lifetime damage rather than ordinary distance despawning. Vexes created with spawn eggs or commands do not take that automatic lifetime damage.

spawn_conditions.answer: Vexes are summoned by an evoker’s attack, not by normal dark-floor spawning. An evoker needs usable nearby summoning positions. Evoker-summoned vexes have a limited lifetime; spawn eggs and commands are different.

experience.answer: A vex gives 5 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Its natural iron sword is not a dropped reward, even with Looting.

equipment_drops.answer: A vex does not drop its naturally held iron sword. Looting does not change that. Its death experience is a separate reward.

attack_style.answer: A vex flies through blocks and lunges at close range, glowing red while attacking.

provocation.answer: Evoker-summoned vexes attack on behalf of their summoner. Their red appearance is an attack state, not a separate breed.

counterplay.answer: A simple solid wall is not a reliable cage because vexes can pass through blocks. Keep track of the evoker and incoming vexes rather than hiding behind one thin wall.

growth.answer: A vex has no normal baby form that grows into an adult. There is no ordinary baby-growth timer or growth food to use for this mob.

relocation.answer: A minecart can carry a vex in Bedrock. Bring an empty cart into contact with it, then use rails and powered rails along a protected route. An active activator rail can eject the passenger. It can still be dangerous while riding; a cart is not taming or protection from its attacks. The cart alone does not guarantee persistence in Bedrock.

identity.answer: A vex is a small flying hostile spirit summoned by evokers. It can pass through blocks and attack with a sword, so ordinary walls are not reliable protection.

behavior.answer: A vex is a small flying hostile spirit summoned by evokers. It can pass through blocks and attack with a sword, so ordinary walls are not reliable protection.

fire.answer: It is immune to ordinary fire and lava damage. That does not protect it from every other kind of damage.

sunlight.answer: Ordinary sunlight does not make it take burning damage. It is fire-immune, although other environmental hazards can still matter.

health.answer: Villagers have 20 health points (10 hearts).

spawning.answer: Villagers generate in villages, and can also come from breeding or curing zombie villagers. Bedrock villages occur in plains, deserts, savannas, snowy plains, taigas and snowy taigas.

drops.answer: Ordinary Bedrock villagers do not provide normal item or experience drops when killed. Obtain their goods by trading.

breeding.answer: Two adult villagers need enough food and an available bed for a baby. Each needs 3 bread or 12 carrots, potatoes or beetroots. Keep suitable beds available and allow the villagers to reach one another.

trading.answer: Villagers take jobs from job-site blocks. A villager already traded with keeps its profession and offers; restocking requires access to its claimed workstation. Babies, nitwits and unemployed villagers do not offer normal profession trades.

taming.answer: Villager cannot be tamed as player-owned pets. You can still ask how to breed them.

variants.answer: Villagers have seven biome appearances, thirteen professions, and unemployed/nitwit states. Biome clothing and profession are separate. A swamp-looking villager is not a separate swamp-exclusive profession.

lightning.answer: Lightning can turn a villager into a witch. Protect villagers from lightning; this conversion is not the zombie-villager curing process.

conversion.answer: A zombie can turn a villager into a zombie villager: 0% on Easy, 50% on Normal and 100% on Hard. Lightning instead makes a witch.

sleeping.answer: Villagers use beds at night. Bed ownership also affects village and breeding mechanics; simply placing a decoration that looks like a house does not assign every bed.

sunlight.answer: Sunlight alone does not make it burn like an exposed zombie or skeleton. Other hazards, such as being out of water or changing dimensions, can still matter for the species.

fire.answer: Without protection, ordinary fire and lava can damage it. Being undead, large, or adapted to a particular biome does not by itself grant fire immunity.

growth.answer: A baby villager normally takes about 20 minutes of active game time to become an adult. Feeding does not speed up its growth. A golden dandelion cannot freeze a baby villager’s age. Riding in a boat or minecart does not stop its normal growth.

age_lock.answer: No. Golden dandelions do not pause villager aging. Baby villagers normally grow into adults during active game time.

spawn_conditions.answer: Villagers originally generate with villages and igloo basements. Empty beds or rebuilt village houses do not spontaneously create replacement villagers. Use breeding existing villagers or curing zombie villagers; babies need a breeding setup, not ordinary hostile-mob spawning conditions.

leashing.answer: No, you cannot attach an ordinary lead to it through normal player interaction.

profession.answer: An unemployed adult can claim an available job-site block to get its matching profession. Babies and nitwits cannot take jobs. Once you trade with a villager, its profession and trades are locked; breaking the workstation does not reroll that traded villager. In Bedrock, another villager can claim the workstation you placed.

restocking.answer: A villager restocks exhausted offers by working at its own claimed workstation, up to twice per day. Check that the correct villager claimed the block and can reach it during working hours. Another nearby workstation of the same type is not automatically its workstation.

breeding_conditions.answer: Villager breeding needs willing adults with enough food and available valid beds in the village. Dropping food is different from feeding an animal directly. If mobGriefing is false, villagers do not pick up food, which can prevent your food-based setup from working.

experience.answer: It gives no experience when killed. Item drops and rewards from other interactions are separate.

experience_breeding.answer: Breeding villagers does not give the player the usual animal-breeding experience reward. Trading with villagers is a separate source of experience.

lifetime.answer: Villagers do not naturally despawn, even outside a village. If one is missing, check escape routes, attacks, conversion and other hazards rather than assuming that walking away deleted it.

relocation.answer: Use a boat or minecart for ordinary transport. You cannot attach an ordinary lead to a villager. At the destination, provide safe housing and check its bed and workstation links rather than assuming they transferred correctly.

breeding_age.answer: No. A baby cannot breed; it must grow into an adult first. Food that helps it grow is not the same as breeding food being used on an adult.

diet.answer: Villagers use bread, carrots, potatoes and beetroot as breeding food in their inventories. Each adult needs 3 bread or 12 carrots, potatoes or beetroot, or an equivalent mixture. Throw food for them to pick up rather than feeding them like cows. Food alone is not enough: the village also needs suitable spare beds. Feeding cannot speed a baby villager’s growth.

attack_style.answer: Villagers do not fight players or defend a village through their own melee attacks. Iron golems provide a separate kind of defense.

provocation.answer: A villager does not hit back, but harming villagers can have consequences for village reputation, trading and golem hostility.

counterplay.answer: Protect villagers with safe housing and barriers. Do not assume a passive villager can protect itself from zombies or raids.

construction.answer: Provide an available grindstone to an eligible unemployed adult villager. Babies and nitwits cannot take that job; prior trading can lock an existing profession.

trading.answer: A weaponsmith trades weapons, depending on its level and selected offers. It needs its claimed grindstone to work and restock; every weaponsmith does not have identical offers.

identity.answer: A nitwit is a villager that cannot take a profession or trade.

construction.answer: A nitwit cannot be assigned a profession by giving it a workstation. Use an eligible unemployed adult instead.

trading.answer: Nitwits do not trade, even when workstations are nearby.

identity.answer: An unemployed adult villager does not currently have a profession.

construction.answer: An eligible unemployed adult can claim an available job-site block. Previous trading can lock a villager’s profession.

trading.answer: An unemployed villager needs to obtain a profession before it offers profession trades.

identity.answer: This villager has the plains biome appearance.

spawning.answer: Look for villagers in the matching village biome, or use the biome-dependent appearance rules when breeding villagers in Bedrock.

variants.answer: Biome clothing is separate from profession. The outfit alone does not tell you the villager’s exact trades.

identity.answer: This villager has the desert biome appearance.

spawning.answer: Look for villagers in the matching village biome, or use the biome-dependent appearance rules when breeding villagers in Bedrock.

variants.answer: Biome clothing is separate from profession. The outfit alone does not tell you the villager’s exact trades.

identity.answer: This villager has the savanna biome appearance.

spawning.answer: Look for villagers in the matching village biome, or use the biome-dependent appearance rules when breeding villagers in Bedrock.

variants.answer: Biome clothing is separate from profession. The outfit alone does not tell you the villager’s exact trades.

identity.answer: This villager has the snow biome appearance.

spawning.answer: Look for villagers in the matching village biome, or use the biome-dependent appearance rules when breeding villagers in Bedrock.

variants.answer: Biome clothing is separate from profession. The outfit alone does not tell you the villager’s exact trades.

identity.answer: This villager has the taiga biome appearance.

spawning.answer: Look for villagers in the matching village biome, or use the biome-dependent appearance rules when breeding villagers in Bedrock.

variants.answer: Biome clothing is separate from profession. The outfit alone does not tell you the villager’s exact trades.

identity.answer: This villager has the swamp biome appearance.

spawning.answer: Swamp and jungle villages do not naturally generate. In Bedrock, breeding villagers in the matching biome can produce that biome appearance.

variants.answer: Biome clothing is separate from profession. The outfit alone does not tell you the villager’s exact trades.

identity.answer: This villager has the jungle biome appearance.

spawning.answer: Swamp and jungle villages do not naturally generate. In Bedrock, breeding villagers in the matching biome can produce that biome appearance.

variants.answer: Biome clothing is separate from profession. The outfit alone does not tell you the villager’s exact trades.

diet_cases.answer: Villagers use bread, carrots, potatoes and beetroot as breeding food in their inventories. Each adult needs 3 bread or 12 carrots, potatoes or beetroot, or an equivalent mixture. Throw food for them to pick up rather than feeding them like cows. Food alone is not enough: the village also needs suitable spare beds. Feeding cannot speed a baby villager’s growth.

Farmers can collect wheat and seeds for farming, but seeds and wheat are not the same as ready breeding food. Farmers can turn wheat into bread; villagers use bread, carrots, potatoes or beetroot for breeding.

health.answer: Vindicators have 24 health points (12 hearts).

spawning.answer: Vindicators generate in woodland mansions and appear in raids. Mansion vindicators do not continually respawn.

drops.answer: Vindicators can drop emeralds and have separate equipment-drop chances. Bedrock raid loot has additional conditions; not every possible item drops from each kill.

combat.answer: Vindicators attack at close range with axes. Keep distance and use solid barriers rather than letting several surround you.

taming.answer: Vindicator cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: You cannot breed a vindicator.

sunlight.answer: Sunlight alone does not make it burn like an exposed zombie or skeleton. Other hazards, such as being out of water or changing dimensions, can still matter for the species.

fire.answer: Without protection, ordinary fire and lava can damage it. Being undead, large, or adapted to a particular biome does not by itself grant fire immunity.

variants.answer: Naming a vindicator Johnny changes its aggression toward many other mobs. It does not tame it or create a new species.

spawn_conditions.answer: Mansion vindicators generate once and do not refill by waiting. Raids provide another source. A dark mansion-shaped building outside the actual generated structure does not create a natural vindicator farm.

experience.answer: The base reward is 5 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Naturally spawned equipment can affect the total; picked-up equipment and whether the gear itself drops are separate conditions. Looting does not multiply experience.

equipment_drops.answer: Naturally spawned weapons or armor are not guaranteed drops. Qualifying player or tamed-wolf kills and Looting can matter. Equipment the mob picked up later is a different category; do not assume one chance covers both. Its ordinary body loot is separate.

attack_style.answer: Vindicators rush targets and use powerful close-range axe attacks. An unarmed vindicator can still attack.

provocation.answer: Vindicators are normally hostile to players, adult villagers and golems. Naming one Johnny makes it attack many additional kinds of mob; it does not make a friendly pet.

counterplay.answer: Keep out of axe range and use ranged attacks or secure barriers. Do not assume a vindicator is harmless when its arms are folded or when it has no visible weapon.

growth.answer: A vindicator has no normal baby form that grows into an adult. There is no ordinary baby-growth timer or growth food to use for this mob.

lifetime.answer: Vindicators normally have persistence in Bedrock and do not disappear through ordinary distance despawning. They can still be killed or removed by other game rules. Raid cleanup and special encounter states are different from keeping an ordinary mob.

relocation.answer: A minecart can carry a vindicator in Bedrock. Bring an empty cart into contact with it, then use rails and powered rails along a protected route. An active activator rail can eject the passenger. It can still be dangerous while riding; a cart is not taming or protection from its attacks. The cart alone does not guarantee persistence in Bedrock.

identity.answer: A vindicator is a hostile axe-wielding illager. It attacks at close range and appears in raids and certain structures.

behavior.answer: A vindicator is a hostile axe-wielding illager. It attacks at close range and appears in raids and certain structures.

health.answer: Wandering traders have 20 health points (10 hearts).

spawning.answer: Wandering traders can appear near players in the Overworld with two trader llamas. They are temporary visitors and can despawn even if named.

drops.answer: Killing a wandering trader does not give its trading inventory. A held drinking or displayed item has separate Bedrock drop chances.

breeding.answer: Wandering traders cannot breed or become ordinary village residents.

trading.answer: Use emeralds to buy the trader’s offered goods. Its offers and stock are limited; it does not take a village profession or restock like a normal villager.

taming.answer: Wandering trader cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

sunlight.answer: Sunlight alone does not make it burn like an exposed zombie or skeleton. Other hazards, such as being out of water or changing dimensions, can still matter for the species.

fire.answer: Without protection, ordinary fire and lava can damage it. Being undead, large, or adapted to a particular biome does not by itself grant fire immunity.

variants.answer: Wandering traders are distinct from ordinary profession villagers. Becoming invisible at night is a behavior, not a new profession.

spawn_conditions.answer: Wandering traders attempt to spawn near players in the Overworld; Bedrock can also try near a claimed village bell. Their appearance is random, not guaranteed on demand. A workstation does not turn a normal villager into a wandering trader.

leashing.answer: No, you cannot attach an ordinary lead to it through normal player interaction.

experience.answer: Killing a wandering trader gives no experience. Successful trading can reward experience in Bedrock; killing it is not the same interaction.

equipment_drops.answer: In Bedrock, a wandering trader holding its milk bucket or Invisibility potion can drop that held consumable when killed: 25%, plus one percentage point per Looting level, up to 28% with Looting III. It must be holding or drinking the item at the time; the two consumables are not both guaranteed drops.

lifetime.answer: A wandering trader can still despawn after its special lifetime even if named or put in a boat or minecart. In Bedrock, the timer and whether players are within 24 blocks matter; exhausting all its trades can also make it leave when players are farther away. Do not plan on a name tag keeping it forever.

relocation.answer: A boat or minecart can move it, but does not stop its special despawn timer. Ordinary leads cannot attach directly to the trader; its llamas have separate lead connections.

growth.answer: A wandering trader has no normal baby form that grows into an adult. There is no ordinary baby-growth timer or growth food to use for this mob.

attack_style.answer: A wandering trader does not attack players. Its trader llamas can defend it by spitting.

provocation.answer: Hitting the trader can provoke its llamas even though the trader itself is passive. Its temporary invisibility is not an attack.

counterplay.answer: Avoid hitting the trader or its llamas. Trade while it is available; trapping or naming it does not remove its special departure timer.

identity.answer: A wandering trader is a travelling merchant that appears with trader llamas. Trade emeralds for its rotating selection of goods before it leaves.

behavior.answer: A wandering trader is a travelling merchant that appears with trader llamas. Trade emeralds for its rotating selection of goods before it leaves.

combat.answer: It does not normally attack players. Trade emeralds for its rotating selection of goods before it leaves.

health.answer: Wardens have 500 health points (250 hearts).

spawning.answer: Wardens emerge after repeated warnings from naturally generated sculk shriekers, usually in the deep dark. They do not use ordinary dark-floor monster spawning.

drops.answer: A warden drops one sculk catalyst and a small amount of experience. Its loot is not a reward worth the danger of fighting it.

combat.answer: Wardens are blind but detect vibrations and smell nearby targets. Sneaking and wool can help manage vibrations. Their powerful melee attacks and ranged sonic boom make avoiding them safer than fighting.

taming.answer: Warden cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: You cannot breed a warden.

vibrations.answer: Wardens detect vibrations and smell nearby targets. Sneaking and wool can help manage vibrations, but do not make a nearby warden permanently unable to detect you.

variants.answer: A warden can emerge, investigate, become angry or dig away. These are behavior states, not animal breeds.

spawn_conditions.answer: A player’s warning level must reach four through naturally generated sculk shriekers. The shrieker needs a valid nearby emergence space. Light level does not control this process. A shrieker collected and placed by a player does not summon a warden like a naturally generated one.

experience.answer: It gives 5 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Looting affects certain item drops, not this experience reward.

attack_style.answer: A warden uses powerful close-range strikes and a sonic boom that passes through blocks. It detects vibrations and can smell targets rather than seeing them.

provocation.answer: Vibrations and nearby targets can raise its anger. Sneaking avoids many movement vibrations, but does not prevent it from smelling you at close range.

counterplay.answer: Avoid triggering shriekers and retreat quietly. Wool can block vibration paths, but does not stop the warden’s smell or sonic boom. Walls, armor and shields are not protection from that sonic attack.

lifetime.answer: An unnamed calm warden can dig away after about 60 seconds without detecting targets or vibrations. Named wardens do not use that ordinary digging-away behavior. It is not governed by the usual distance-based monster despawn checks.

growth.answer: A warden has no normal baby form that grows into an adult. There is no ordinary baby-growth timer or growth food to use for this mob.

relocation.answer: You cannot transport a warden as an ordinary minecart passenger or by attaching a normal lead. Luring it by sounds is dangerous and is not taming or safe transport.

identity.answer: The Warden is a powerful hostile mob associated with the deep dark and sculk shriekers. It uses vibrations, smell, and a sonic attack to find and fight threats. Sneak away and avoid summoning it rather than treating it as an ordinary fight.

behavior.answer: The Warden is a powerful hostile mob associated with the deep dark and sculk shriekers. It uses vibrations, smell, and a sonic attack to find and fight threats. Sneak away and avoid summoning it rather than treating it as an ordinary fight.

fire.answer: It is immune to ordinary fire and lava damage. That does not protect it from every other kind of damage.

sunlight.answer: Ordinary sunlight does not make it take burning damage. It is fire-immune, although other environmental hazards can still matter.

spawning.answer: Wind-charge projectiles come from breezes or from using a wind charge item, depending on the projectile type.

interactions.answer: Wind charges burst on impact, pushing entities and interacting with some buttons, doors and other mechanisms. Player wind charges and breeze projectiles do not have identical rules.

projectile_use.answer: Throw a wind charge to create a burst of wind on impact. It can activate supported buttons, doors, trapdoors and other mechanisms.

projectile_effects.answer: A direct hit deals a small amount of damage and knockback; the burst also pushes nearby entities. A careless launch can cause a dangerous fall.

retrieval.answer: A thrown wind charge is consumed. It is not a dropped breeze rod that can be collected after the burst.

identity.answer: A wind charge is a projectile that creates a gust on impact. Use wind bursts for movement tricks and activating compatible mechanisms; be careful about landing damage.

behavior.answer: A wind charge is a projectile that creates a gust on impact. Use wind bursts for movement tricks and activating compatible mechanisms; be careful about landing damage.

health.answer: Witches have 26 health points (13 hearts).

spawning.answer: Find witches in dark Overworld areas, swamp huts and raids. Lightning can also turn a villager into a witch.

drops.answer: Witches can drop redstone and items from pools including sticks, bottles, glowstone dust, gunpowder, spider eyes and sugar. A potion being drunk has a separate drop chance; these are not all guaranteed from every witch.

combat.answer: Witches throw harmful splash potions and drink potions to heal or protect themselves. Keep your distance and avoid staying inside their throwing range.

taming.answer: Witch cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: You cannot breed a witch.

fire.answer: Witches can use Fire Resistance potions, which can protect them from fire or lava for a time. They are not unconditionally fire-immune in every state.

variants.answer: Witches may drink potions and can appear naturally or in raids. Drinking and potion effects are states, not separate species.

spawn_conditions.answer: Bedrock witches avoid natural spawning in mushroom fields, deep dark, rivers, frozen rivers and snowy plains. Swamp huts use a particular hardcoded spawning spot. Raid spawning and lightning conversion are separate routes.

experience.answer: It gives 5 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Looting affects certain item drops, not this experience reward.

equipment_drops.answer: In Bedrock, killing a witch while it is drinking a potion can drop that potion if a player or tamed wolf gets kill credit. The chance is 25%, plus one percentage point per Looting level, up to 28% with Looting III. It is the potion being drunk, not every potion the witch can use.

attack_style.answer: A witch throws harmful splash potions and can drink potions to heal or protect itself.

provocation.answer: Witches are hostile to players. A witch pausing to drink is not becoming friendly or offering that potion to you.

counterplay.answer: Use cover and keep track of poison and other effects. Milk removes status effects but does not prevent another potion hit, and also clears useful effects you may want to keep.

growth.answer: A witch has no normal baby form that grows into an adult. There is no ordinary baby-growth timer or growth food to use for this mob.

lifetime.answer: A naturally spawned witch can disappear through ordinary distance despawning unless it has become persistent. In Bedrock, a name tag is one way to prevent ordinary distance despawning; distance rules depend on simulation settings and mob state. Raid-spawned mobs have special persistence, and encounter cleanup is a separate rule. A boat or minecart alone is not a blanket persistence guarantee, and persistence does not prevent death.

relocation.answer: A minecart can carry a witch in Bedrock. Bring an empty cart into contact with it, then use rails and powered rails along a protected route. An active activator rail can eject the passenger. It can still be dangerous while riding; a cart is not taming or protection from its attacks. The cart alone does not guarantee persistence in Bedrock.

identity.answer: A witch is a hostile potion-using mob. It throws harmful potions and drinks useful potions to protect or heal itself.

behavior.answer: A witch is a hostile potion-using mob. It throws harmful potions and drinks useful potions to protect or heal itself.

health.answer: In Bedrock, the wither has 300 health points on Easy, 450 on Normal and 600 on Hard.

construction.answer: Build a T from four soul sand or soul soil blocks, then put three wither skeleton skulls across its top. Place the last skull last and leave the required space clear. It cannot be summoned on Peaceful.

spawning.answer: Players summon the wither using soul sand or soul soil and three wither skeleton skulls; it does not naturally wander into the world.

drops.answer: Defeating the wither drops a nether star. Bedrock also awards 50 experience, and the dropped nether star does not normally despawn.

combat.answer: The Bedrock wither fires explosive skulls and becomes more dangerous during its later phase. Prepare a secure fighting area and healing.

taming.answer: Wither cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: You cannot breed a wither. They are created using their construction or summoning method instead.

powder_snow.answer: The wither is immune to ordinary powder-snow freezing damage. This does not imply that every other kind of damage is ineffective.

variants.answer: The Wither changes its attack behavior during the fight, including its armored phase. Difficulty also affects the Bedrock fight; these are not biome breeds.

spawn_conditions.answer: Summon the Wither using four soul sand or soul soil blocks and three wither skeleton skulls in the Wither construction arrangement, placing a skull last and leaving the required spaces clear. It does not naturally appear in a Nether biome, and Peaceful prevents the fight.

experience.answer: In Bedrock the Wither gives 50 experience points regardless of how it dies. This is experience, separate from its Nether star.

attack_style.answer: The wither fires explosive skulls that can inflict Wither. In Bedrock, its later phase includes destructive dash attacks and an explosion when it reaches half health.

provocation.answer: The wither is a hostile boss once its spawning sequence finishes. Its initial charge-up ends in an explosion, and it also explodes during its death sequence.

counterplay.answer: Fight away from buildings and prepare for explosions and Wither damage. At half health it gains anti-projectile armor, so ordinary arrows stop being a reliable attack; prepare a close-range weapon for the later phase. Keep clear during the final death explosion.

growth.answer: A wither has no normal baby form that grows into an adult. There is no ordinary baby-growth timer or growth food to use for this mob.

lifetime.answer: Withers normally have persistence in Bedrock and do not disappear through ordinary distance despawning. They can still be killed or removed by other game rules.

relocation.answer: You cannot transport a wither as an ordinary minecart passenger or by attaching a normal lead. Its boss encounter is not a normal tame-and-transport interaction.

identity.answer: The Wither is a powerful summoned undead boss. It flies, fires explosive skulls, and causes destructive fights. Defeating it provides a Nether star.

behavior.answer: The Wither is a powerful summoned undead boss. It flies, fires explosive skulls, and causes destructive fights. Defeating it provides a Nether star.

fire.answer: It is immune to ordinary fire and lava damage. That does not protect it from every other kind of damage.

sunlight.answer: Ordinary sunlight does not make it take burning damage. It is fire-immune, although other environmental hazards can still matter.

water.answer: It can breathe underwater.

health.answer: Wither skeletons have 20 health points (10 hearts).

spawning.answer: Look in Nether fortresses. In Bedrock, the Wither can also produce wither skeletons during its fight on Normal or Hard difficulty.

drops.answer: Wither skeletons can drop coal and bones. A player or tamed-wolf kill has a 2.5% skull chance; in Bedrock each Looting level adds 2 percentage points, reaching 8.5% with Looting III. A charged-creeper kill can also produce a skull. Equipment has separate chances.

combat.answer: Their melee attacks inflict Wither. Keep distance or use a barrier that takes advantage of their height.

taming.answer: Wither skeleton cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: You cannot breed a wither skeleton.

variants.answer: A wither skeleton is a separate Nether skeleton-type mob, not an ordinary skeleton that grew older.

spawn_conditions.answer: Natural wither-skeleton spawning needs a fortress spawning area, light level 0–7 and enough room for the tall mob. Within overall fortress bounds but outside individual fortress pieces, Nether-brick flooring matters. A Nether-brick platform outside a fortress is not sufficient.

experience.answer: The base reward is 5 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Naturally spawned equipment can affect the total; picked-up equipment and whether the gear itself drops are separate conditions. Looting does not multiply experience.

equipment_drops.answer: Naturally spawned weapons or armor are not guaranteed drops. Qualifying player or tamed-wolf kills and Looting can matter. Equipment the mob picked up later is a different category; do not assume one chance covers both. Its ordinary body loot is separate.

attack_style.answer: A wither skeleton attacks at close range with its sword and can inflict the Wither effect.

provocation.answer: Wither skeletons are hostile; they do not need you to attack first. They are different from ordinary bow-using skeletons.

counterplay.answer: Use cover and space that accounts for their tall body. Milk can clear Wither, but unlike ordinary Poison the Wither effect can be fatal; another hit can apply it again.

growth.answer: A wither skeleton has no normal baby form that grows into an adult. There is no ordinary baby-growth timer or growth food to use for this mob.

lifetime.answer: A naturally spawned wither skeleton can disappear through ordinary distance despawning unless it has become persistent. In Bedrock, a name tag is one way to prevent ordinary distance despawning; distance rules depend on simulation settings and mob state. A boat or minecart alone is not a blanket persistence guarantee, and persistence does not prevent death.

relocation.answer: A minecart can carry a wither skeleton in Bedrock. Bring an empty cart into contact with it, then use rails and powered rails along a protected route. An active activator rail can eject the passenger. It can still be dangerous while riding; a cart is not taming or protection from its attacks. The cart alone does not guarantee persistence in Bedrock.

identity.answer: A wither skeleton is a hostile Nether skeleton that usually fights with a sword. Its attacks inflict the Wither effect, and its rare skull drop is used to summon the Wither.

behavior.answer: A wither skeleton is a hostile Nether skeleton that usually fights with a sword. Its attacks inflict the Wither effect, and its rare skull drop is used to summon the Wither.

fire.answer: It is immune to ordinary fire and lava damage. That does not protect it from every other kind of damage.

sunlight.answer: Ordinary sunlight does not make it take burning damage. It is fire-immune, although other environmental hazards can still matter.

water.answer: It can breathe underwater.

spawning.answer: The wither launches wither-skull projectiles during combat.

combat.answer: Wither skulls explode on impact and can apply Wither. The slower blue skull has stronger block-breaking properties than an ordinary black skull.

projectile_use.answer: The Wither fires explosive skull projectiles. These are separate from the wither skeleton skull item used for summoning.

projectile_effects.answer: Wither skull impacts can explode and inflict Wither. The blue dangerous variant has different block-breaking behavior from an ordinary black skull.

retrieval.answer: A fired wither skull is not a collectible wither skeleton head. Defeating a wither skeleton under its head-drop conditions is a separate task.

identity.answer: A Wither skull projectile is an explosive attack fired by the Wither. Avoid the impact and resulting harmful effects; it is not the same thing as a collectible wither skeleton skull.

behavior.answer: A Wither skull projectile is an explosive attack fired by the Wither. Avoid the impact and resulting harmful effects; it is not the same thing as a collectible wither skeleton skull.

spawning.answer: The wither launches wither-skull projectiles during combat.

combat.answer: Wither skulls explode on impact and can apply Wither. The slower blue skull has stronger block-breaking properties than an ordinary black skull.

projectile_use.answer: The Wither fires explosive skull projectiles. These are separate from the wither skeleton skull item used for summoning.

projectile_effects.answer: Wither skull impacts can explode and inflict Wither. The blue dangerous variant has different block-breaking behavior from an ordinary black skull.

retrieval.answer: A fired wither skull is not a collectible wither skeleton head. Defeating a wither skeleton under its head-drop conditions is a separate task.

identity.answer: A blue Wither skull is a dangerous variant of the Wither's explosive projectile. It can break blocks that resist many ordinary explosions, so do not rely on a simple wall for protection.

behavior.answer: A blue Wither skull is a dangerous variant of the Wither's explosive projectile. It can break blocks that resist many ordinary explosions, so do not rely on a simple wall for protection.

health.answer: Wild Bedrock wolves have 8 health points (4 hearts); tamed wolves have 40 health points (20 hearts).

spawning.answer: Wolf coats depend on the biome: pale in taiga, ashen in snowy taiga, black in old growth pine taiga, chestnut in old growth spruce taiga, rusty in sparse jungle, snowy in grove, spotted in savanna plateau, striped in wooded badlands and woods in forest.

variants.answer: There are nine wolf variants: pale, woods, ashen, black, chestnut, rusty, spotted, striped and snowy. Their home biomes differ. A baby inherits a parent’s variant rather than changing to match the breeding biome.

drops.answer: Wolves have no ordinary meat or fur drop. Equipped wolf armor drops separately. Experience depends on age and the kill conditions.

taming.answer: Feed bones to a wild, non-angry wolf. Each bone has a one-in-three chance to tame it. A wolf already owned by another player cannot be tamed again.

breeding.answer: Feed meat to two standing, tamed adult wolves at full health. Rotten flesh and raw chicken work. Bedrock has a one-minute breeding cooldown.

interactions.answer: Tamed wolves follow their owner or can sit. Meat heals them, dyes change their collars, and wolf armor provides protection.

combat.answer: Wild wolves can become hostile when provoked, and nearby wolves may join the attack. A tamed wolf can fight for its owner. Ownership and the current anger state matter; a wolf is not always harmless.

fire.answer: Without protection, it can take fire and lava damage and die. Living in a warm biome or having a particular coat color does not grant fire immunity.

sunlight.answer: Ordinary sunlight does not make this creature spontaneously burn. Fire, lava and lightning are separate hazards.

water.answer: It needs air and can drown if trapped fully underwater. Being able to swim or float is not the same as being able to breathe underwater.

powder_snow.answer: It can take freezing damage while trapped in powder snow without applicable protection. A cold-biome home or white coat alone does not guarantee freezing immunity.

equipment.answer: Wolf armor uses armadillo scutes. The owner can equip suitable armor, dye it, repair it with scutes, and remove it with shears under the appropriate interaction. Armor and collar dye are separate.

repair.answer: Repair equipped wolf armor with armadillo scutes. Feeding meat heals the wolf; repairing armor and restoring the wolf’s own health are different actions.

anger.answer: Wild wolves can become angry when attacked and nearby wolves may join. A tamed wolf can defend its owner. Meat is for a tamed wolf’s feeding uses; bones are for taming.

land.answer: It can live on land. Still provide suitable safe terrain and protect it from fire, falls or other species-specific hazards.

age_lock.answer: Use a golden dandelion on an eligible baby to pause its aging. Use another golden dandelion on that same baby to resume aging. This is separate from feeding normal food to speed growth.

spawn_conditions.answer: Check the natural habitat of the coat you want and a suitable surface such as grass, coarse dirt, snow, snow blocks or podzol. A spawn egg’s biome-selected coat does not prove wolves naturally spawn in every biome with that coat. Wolves near biome borders can differ.

leashing.answer: You can attach a lead while it is not angry. If it becomes angry while already leashed, that alone does not break the lead, but you cannot reattach one while it remains angry. Leashing does not tame it.

sitting.answer: As its owner, use the tamed creature to switch between sitting and standing. Sitting keeps it from normally following you; it does not grant invulnerability. Use an empty hand to avoid a food or equipment interaction instead.

collar.answer: After taming a wolf, its owner can use dye to change its collar color. The collar color does not change the wolf’s natural coat variant.

experience.answer: An adult wolf normally gives 1–3 experience points after an eligible player or tamed-wolf kill. In Bedrock, a tamed wolf killed by its own owner gives no experience. Baby wolves give none.

experience_baby.answer: A baby wolf gives no experience when killed.

experience_breeding.answer: Successful breeding gives 1–7 experience points. That reward comes from breeding, not from killing the baby. The animal’s own breeding requirements still apply.

attack_style.answer: Wild angry wolves bite at close range. Tamed wolves can defend their owner and attack some targets for them.

provocation.answer: Hitting a wild wolf can anger it and nearby wolves. Tamed wolves have owner-related behavior; taming is different from merely giving an angry wolf another food.

counterplay.answer: Do not provoke a wild pack. Tamed wolves do not normally attack creepers or ghasts for you, so keep them away from explosions and do not assume they counter every hostile mob.

lifetime.answer: Wolves do not naturally despawn, and a tamed wolf remains yours when you leave. Missing from sight is not proof of despawning: it may be sitting, blocked, outside loaded chunks or dead. Taming does not protect it from ordinary hazards.

relocation.answer: Tame it and let it follow while standing, or use a lead while it is calm. Sitting stops normal following. Do not assume teleporting will rescue it from every unloaded area, dimension boundary or hazard.

teleportation.answer: A tamed pet that is standing can follow and teleport closer when far enough away if a valid destination is available. Sitting and other travel states can prevent normal following. Do not assume it can teleport out of an unloaded area or automatically cross dimensions; move carefully and check it arrives.

breeding_age.answer: No. A baby cannot breed; it must grow into an adult first. Food that helps it grow is not the same as breeding food being used on an adult.

breeding_ownership.answer: The parents must be tamed before breeding. Use eligible adult animals and their breeding food; feeding wild animals is not enough to skip taming.

breeding_health.answer: Both tamed adult wolves must be at full health before breeding. Feed suitable meat to heal them first, then use breeding food while they are standing.

growth.answer: A baby wolf normally takes about 20 minutes of active game time to become an adult. You can speed this up by feeding it suitable meat such as beef or rotten flesh, not fish.

diet.answer: Bones tame wild, non-angry wolves. Meat such as beef or rotten flesh can breed tamed adults and help pups grow. Meat, fish and rabbit stew have healing uses in Bedrock, but fish and rabbit stew do not breed wolves. Food for healing is not automatically food for taming or breeding.

identity.answer: A wolf is a neutral animal that can be tamed into a companion. Tame it with bones, then have it follow or sit. Tamed wolves help defend their owner and can wear wolf armor.

behavior.answer: A wolf is a neutral animal that can be tamed into a companion. Tame it with bones, then have it follow or sit. Tamed wolves help defend their owner and can wear wolf armor.

spawning.answer: Look for pale wolves in the taiga biome.
Look for woods wolves in the forest biome.
Look for ashen wolves in the snowy taiga biome.
Look for black wolves in the old growth pine taiga biome.
Look for chestnut wolves in the old growth spruce taiga biome.
Look for rusty wolves in the sparse jungle biome.
Look for spotted wolves in the savanna plateau biome.
Look for striped wolves in the wooded badlands biome.
Look for snowy wolves in the grove biome.
Throw a bottle o’ enchanting or dispense it to create the projectile.

interactions.answer: The bottle breaks on impact and releases experience orbs. It does not directly apply an enchantment to an item.

projectile_use.answer: Throw the bottle to shatter it and release experience orbs. It is not a bottle that stores your current player level.

projectile_effects.answer: A bottle gives 3–11 experience points on impact, averaging seven. Points and player levels are different quantities.

retrieval.answer: The thrown bottle is consumed when it breaks. The reward is collected as experience orbs, not as an empty reusable bottle.

experience.answer: A bottle gives 3–11 experience points on impact, averaging seven. Points and player levels are different quantities.

identity.answer: A bottle o' enchanting is a throwable item that releases experience. Throw it to create experience orbs for levels or suitable Mending equipment.

behavior.answer: A bottle o' enchanting is a throwable item that releases experience. Throw it to create experience orbs for levels or suitable Mending equipment.

spawning.answer: Experience orbs come from activities such as suitable mob kills, mining certain ores, smelting, breeding and trading.

interactions.answer: Nearby experience orbs move toward players and are collected for experience. Mending can use collected experience to repair eligible equipment.

experience.answer: Experience orbs carry experience points, not whole player levels. Orbs can have different values; collecting one orb is not always exactly one point.

retrieval.answer: Move close enough to collect experience. Eligible equipped Mending items can use collected experience to repair durability instead of all of it going to your level.

storage.answer: Experience orbs are not inventory items you can store in a normal chest. Bottles o’ enchanting are a different item and do not bottle your existing level.

identity.answer: An experience orb is a small entity that players collect for experience. It contributes toward experience levels or repairs suitable equipped Mending items.

behavior.answer: An experience orb is a small entity that players collect for experience. It contributes toward experience levels or repairs suitable equipped Mending items.

health.answer: Zoglins have 40 health points (20 hearts).

spawning.answer: A hoglin becomes a zoglin after spending 15 seconds outside the Nether. Zoglins are not a normal biome-spawning herd.

drops.answer: Zoglins can drop 1–3 rotten flesh, including babies, with applicable Looting increases.

breeding.answer: Zoglins cannot be bred.

taming.answer: Zoglins cannot be tamed.

combat.answer: Zoglins attack many nearby creatures, including players. Do not treat one as a living hoglin that can be controlled with fungi.

conversion.answer: A zoglin does not normally convert back to a hoglin. It cannot be restored by the zombie-villager curing method.

variants.answer: Zoglins can be babies or adults after hoglins zombify. They do not breed with food like ordinary hoglins.

spawn_conditions.answer: Conversion requires a hoglin outside the Nether for 15 seconds. Lighting a platform or breeding zoglins does not create more of them.

leashing.answer: Yes. Use a lead on it to move it, then use a fence to tie it there. You can remove the lead with shears. Leashing does not tame the creature or give it immunity to hazards.

experience.answer: Both adults and babies give 5 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Do not apply the usual baby-animal zero-experience rule here.

experience_baby.answer: A baby gives 5 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill, just like an adult.

attack_style.answer: A zoglin rushes nearby targets and attacks at close range. It is an undead mob, not an ordinary tameable hoglin.

provocation.answer: Zoglins attack many nearby creatures and players. Hoglin breeding food does not make them friendly.

counterplay.answer: Keep your distance and contain it with solid barriers. Do not rely on the warped-fungus repellent used for ordinary hoglins; zoglins behave differently.

growth.answer: Baby zoglins never grow into adults. A baby hoglin can grow while it remains a hoglin, but converting it into a zoglin does not preserve that normal growth cycle.

lifetime.answer: A naturally spawned zoglin can disappear through ordinary distance despawning unless it has become persistent. In Bedrock, a name tag is one way to prevent ordinary distance despawning; distance rules depend on simulation settings and mob state. A boat or minecart alone is not a blanket persistence guarantee, and persistence does not prevent death.

relocation.answer: You can use a lead to move a zoglin. Guide it along a safe route, keep it close enough that the lead does not break, and protect it from falls and unsuitable water or heat. A lead does not make this hostile mob safe to approach.

identity.answer: A zoglin is an undead hoglin variant created when a hoglin transforms outside the Nether. It is aggressive toward many nearby entities and cannot be bred like an ordinary hoglin.

behavior.answer: A zoglin is an undead hoglin variant created when a hoglin transforms outside the Nether. It is aggressive toward many nearby entities and cannot be bred like an ordinary hoglin.

fire.answer: It is immune to ordinary fire and lava damage. That does not protect it from every other kind of damage.

sunlight.answer: Ordinary sunlight does not make it take burning damage. It is fire-immune, although other environmental hazards can still matter.

water.answer: It can breathe underwater.

health.answer: Bedrock zombies have 20 health points (10 hearts).

spawning.answer: Zombies appear in suitable dark Overworld areas and from monster or trial spawners. Deserts often produce husks instead.

drops.answer: Zombies can drop 0–2 rotten flesh, with rare iron ingot, carrot or potato drops under player-kill conditions. Equipment has separate rules. A charged-creeper kill can produce a zombie head.

interactions.answer: Zombies burn in daylight unless protected. They can infect villagers: the conversion chance is 0% on Easy, 50% on Normal and 100% on Hard. A submerged zombie can become a drowned.

taming.answer: Zombie cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: You cannot breed a zombie.

conversion.answer: An ordinary zombie kept submerged can convert into a drowned. A zombie killing a villager can instead infect that villager, with the chance depending on difficulty; these are separate mechanics.

fire.answer: Without protection, ordinary fire and lava can damage it. Being undead, large, or adapted to a particular biome does not by itself grant fire immunity.

growth.answer: Baby undead of this kind do not normally grow into adults while they remain undead. A cured baby zombie villager can later grow as a living villager.

variants.answer: Zombies can be babies or adults. Husks, drowned and zombie villagers have their own mechanics; curing applies to zombie villagers, not ordinary zombies.

spawn_conditions.answer: Natural zombies need a suitable dark solid spawning surface and two blocks of height, even for babies. Bedrock excludes mushroom fields, deep dark, rivers, frozen rivers and snowy plains. Desert husks, drowned conversion and zombie-villager generation are separate mechanics.

experience.answer: The base reward is 5 experience points for an adult or 12 for a baby after an eligible player or tamed-wolf kill. Naturally spawned equipment can add experience; items picked up later are a separate category.

experience_baby.answer: The base baby reward is 12 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Naturally spawned equipment can add more; this is different from ordinary baby animals giving no experience.

equipment_drops.answer: Naturally spawned weapons or armor are not guaranteed drops. Qualifying player or tamed-wolf kills and Looting can matter. Equipment the mob picked up later is a different category; do not assume one chance covers both. Its ordinary body loot is separate.

attack_style.answer: Zombies normally chase targets and deal close-range melee damage. Some can carry weapons, and babies are faster than adults.

provocation.answer: Zombies are hostile without needing to be hit first. They also threaten villagers, so a village wall is useful even when no player is fighting.

counterplay.answer: Keep distance and use barriers or ranged attacks. Light and secure a village rather than relying on villagers to escape; sunlight is not reliable protection against babies wearing cover or zombies in shade.

lifetime.answer: A naturally spawned zombie can disappear through ordinary distance despawning unless it has become persistent. In Bedrock, a name tag is one way to prevent ordinary distance despawning; distance rules depend on simulation settings and mob state. A boat or minecart alone is not a blanket persistence guarantee, and persistence does not prevent death.

relocation.answer: A minecart can carry a zombie in Bedrock. Bring an empty cart into contact with it, then use rails and powered rails along a protected route. An active activator rail can eject the passenger. It can still be dangerous while riding; a cart is not taming or protection from its attacks. The cart alone does not guarantee persistence in Bedrock.

identity.answer: A zombie is a hostile undead mob that attacks at close range. It normally burns in direct sunlight unless protected and can transform into a drowned after suitable underwater conditions.

behavior.answer: A zombie is a hostile undead mob that attacks at close range. It normally burns in direct sunlight unless protected and can transform into a drowned after suitable underwater conditions.

combat.answer: It is a hostile mob and can attack players. It normally burns in direct sunlight unless protected and can transform into a drowned after suitable underwater conditions.

sunlight.answer: It can burn in direct sunlight when unprotected. Shade, water and applicable armor protection can prevent that; sunlight protection does not make it immune to lava.

water.answer: It can breathe underwater. It can also breathe air.

health.answer: Zombie horses have 25 health points.

spawning.answer: Zombie horsemen can appear at night or during thunderstorms in suitable plains and savanna biomes and snowy plains; Bedrock also includes ice spikes. The mounted zombie is a separate entity.

drops.answer: Zombie horses can drop 2–3 rotten flesh plus applicable equipped items. The rider has separate loot.

taming.answer: Repeatedly ride a zombie horse until it accepts you, then use suitable equipment to control it.

breeding.answer: Zombie horses cannot be bred.

combat.answer: The zombie horse itself is passive, but a mounted zombie is a separate hostile opponent. Deal with the rider without assuming the horse is making the attack.

equipment.answer: Tame the zombie horse by riding, then use the appropriate saddle and armor equipment. Its zombie rider is a separate hostile creature; body armor can protect the horse from sunlight.

fire.answer: Without protection, ordinary fire and lava can damage it. Being undead, large, or adapted to a particular biome does not by itself grant fire immunity.

variants.answer: A zombie horse is a different undead horse mob from a skeleton horse. Its rider and equipment are separate from its identity.

spawn_conditions.answer: Natural zombie horsemen require grass in eligible plains, savanna or snowy-plains habitats, suitable darkness and a difficulty allowing monsters. They arrive as a zombie rider and horse, not ordinary passive horse herds. Snow blocks can prevent the grass-based spawning route.

leashing.answer: You can attach a lead once it is not being ridden by a hostile mob. Deal with the hostile rider first; the mount and rider are separate creatures.

experience.answer: An adult can drop 1–3 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Babies do not give death experience. These are experience points, not player levels.

experience_baby.answer: The baby does not give experience when killed. Growing into an adult changes its death reward; it is separate from experience earned by successful breeding.

lifetime.answer: A wild zombie horse can despawn until player interaction makes it persistent. Its zombie rider is a separate mob. Keeping the horse does not protect it from fire, damage or other hazards.

diet.answer: Feed red mushrooms to heal a zombie horse. It uses a different feeding interaction from a living horse, and red mushrooms do not make zombie horses breed.

growth.answer: Zombie horses cannot breed, so they have no normal breeding-and-raising cycle. I do not have a growth time to give you for a command-created baby.

relocation.answer: You can use a lead to move a zombie horse. Guide it along a safe route, keep it close enough that the lead does not break, and protect it from falls and unsuitable water or heat. Remove hostile riders before trying to attach the lead; a hostile rider is a separate opponent.

attack_style.answer: A zombie horse itself does not damage players, but its zombie rider can attack while mounted. The rider controls a separate hostile part of the encounter.

provocation.answer: The riderless zombie horse is passive. A hostile rider making the mount approach you does not turn the horse itself into the source of the weapon attack.

counterplay.answer: Deal with the zombie rider before taming or riding the horse. A red mushroom heals the mount; it is not a way to pacify the zombie rider.

identity.answer: A zombie horse is an undead horse variant. Its availability and riding rules depend on the game version and how it was obtained; do not assume ordinary horse breeding works.

behavior.answer: A zombie horse is an undead horse variant. Its availability and riding rules depend on the game version and how it was obtained; do not assume ordinary horse breeding works.

sunlight.answer: It can burn in direct sunlight when unprotected. Suitable body armor can protect it from sunlight; that is different from fire or lava immunity.

water.answer: It can breathe underwater.

health.answer: Zombie nautiluses have 15 health points.

spawning.answer: Look for trident-wielding adult drowned riding zombie nautiluses in oceans and dripstone caves. Warm-ocean examples have the coral appearance.

drops.answer: Zombie nautiluses can drop rotten flesh and applicable equipped items. A drowned rider has its own separate loot.

taming.answer: Feed pufferfish or a bucket of pufferfish to a zombie nautilus. Each feeding has a one-in-three taming chance.

variants.answer: Zombie nautiluses have ordinary and coral forms; the coral form is associated with warm oceans.

breeding.answer: You cannot breed a zombie nautilus.

combat.answer: Untamed zombie nautiluses can retaliate with a dash and attack pufferfish; tamed ones are normally passive. A drowned rider can make the pair dangerous even though the mount and rider are separate entities.

equipment.answer: A tamed adult uses a saddle for riding and can wear nautilus armor. Treat its rider and mount as separate entities if it originally spawned with a drowned.

fire.answer: Without protection, ordinary fire and lava can damage it. Being undead, large, or adapted to a particular biome does not by itself grant fire immunity.

spawn_conditions.answer: An eligible trident-wielding adult drowned outside river and frozen-river biomes has a chance to generate mounted on a zombie nautilus. It is not made by leaving an ordinary nautilus underwater. Structure-generated drowned are another eligible route.

leashing.answer: A zombie nautilus must not be angry or ridden by a hostile mob before you attach a lead. Remove the drowned rider and let the mount become calm first. Leashing it does not tame it.

experience.answer: It drops 1–3 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. These are experience points, not player levels.

equipment_drops.answer: A zombie nautilus drops its equipped saddle and nautilus armor when killed, if present. The drowned rider’s equipment is a separate mob’s loot.

lifetime.answer: A naturally spawned zombie nautilus can despawn unless made persistent by player interaction; structure-generated ones are already persistent. The drowned rider is a separate mob, so keeping the mount does not automatically preserve the rider.

relocation.answer: Remove the hostile drowned rider, let the mount become calm, then tame and saddle it for riding or attach a lead. The rider and mount are separate; keep the travel route underwater and safe.

diet.answer: Pufferfish or a bucket of pufferfish can tame a zombie nautilus. Other fish and buckets of fish can heal it, but healing food is not automatically taming food. Zombie nautiluses do not breed like living nautiluses.

growth.answer: A zombie nautilus has no normal baby form that grows into an adult. There is no ordinary baby-growth timer or growth food to use for this mob.

attack_style.answer: An untamed zombie nautilus can retaliate with a dash and attacks pufferfish; tamed ones are normally passive. A drowned riding it attacks separately.

provocation.answer: Hitting a wild zombie nautilus can provoke it. A drowned rider may make the pair hostile even when the mount itself would otherwise be passive.

counterplay.answer: Remove a hostile rider before handling the mount and avoid its dash path. Tame the mount with pufferfish when safe; taming it does not tame its drowned rider.

identity.answer: A zombie nautilus is an undead aquatic nautilus variant. It can carry riders and has taming and saddling interactions under suitable conditions. Its undead behavior differs from an ordinary nautilus.

behavior.answer: A zombie nautilus is an undead aquatic nautilus variant. It can carry riders and has taming and saddling interactions under suitable conditions. Its undead behavior differs from an ordinary nautilus.

sunlight.answer: It can burn in direct sunlight when unprotected. Suitable body armor can protect it from sunlight; that is different from fire or lava immunity.

water.answer: It can breathe underwater. It can also breathe air.

identity.answer: This is the coral zombie-nautilus appearance.

spawning.answer: Look for the coral zombie-nautilus form in warm oceans under the drowned-jockey spawning rules. The drowned rider is separate from the mount.

health.answer: Bedrock zombified piglins have 20 health points (10 hearts).

spawning.answer: Zombified piglins appear in suitable Nether areas, near active Overworld Nether portals, from pigs struck by lightning, or when piglins remain outside the Nether.

drops.answer: They can drop rotten flesh and gold nuggets, with rare gold ingots under player-kill conditions. Equipped weapons have separate chances.

interactions.answer: Zombified piglins are usually neutral until provoked, then nearby members can become angry. They do not barter with gold and cannot be cured back into piglins.

taming.answer: Zombie pigman cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: You cannot breed a zombie pigman.

conversion.answer: Zombified piglins do not normally convert back to piglins. Weakness and a golden apple are the zombie-villager cure, not a piglin cure.

anger.answer: Zombified piglins are normally neutral until provoked. Attacking one can make nearby members hostile; gold armor does not cancel that anger.

growth.answer: Baby undead of this kind do not normally grow into adults while they remain undead. A cured baby zombie villager can later grow as a living villager.

variants.answer: Zombified piglins can be babies or adults. They are a different mob from living piglins and piglin brutes.

spawn_conditions.answer: Zombified piglins can appear naturally in eligible Nether areas, from Overworld Nether portals, or from conversions such as piglin zombification and lightning hitting a pig. They do not naturally spawn in Peaceful. A mob travelling through a portal is different from a portal generating one.

experience.answer: The base reward is 5 experience points for an adult or 12 for a baby after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Naturally spawned equipment that is not dropped can add experience.

experience_baby.answer: A baby zombified piglin gives a base 12 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill, with equipment-related conditions separate.

attack_style.answer: An angry zombified piglin closes in and attacks with its weapon. Nearby zombified piglins can join the fight.

provocation.answer: They normally ignore players, but attacking one can provoke nearby group members. Gold armor is not a way to cancel that anger.

counterplay.answer: Avoid hitting one while fighting other mobs. If a group becomes angry, retreat to cover rather than treating each piglin as an isolated opponent.

lifetime.answer: A naturally spawned zombie pigman can disappear through ordinary distance despawning unless it has become persistent. In Bedrock, a name tag is one way to prevent ordinary distance despawning; distance rules depend on simulation settings and mob state. A boat or minecart alone is not a blanket persistence guarantee, and persistence does not prevent death.

relocation.answer: A minecart can carry a zombie pigman in Bedrock. Bring an empty cart into contact with it, then use rails and powered rails along a protected route. An active activator rail can eject the passenger. A small minority of zombified piglins refuse minecart boarding, so a particular one may not enter. It can still be dangerous while riding; a cart is not taming or protection from its attacks. The cart alone does not guarantee persistence in Bedrock.

identity.answer: A zombified piglin is a neutral undead Nether mob. Attacking one can anger nearby zombified piglins. It does not barter like an ordinary piglin.

behavior.answer: A zombified piglin is a neutral undead Nether mob. Attacking one can anger nearby zombified piglins. It does not barter like an ordinary piglin.

combat.answer: It can attack under particular conditions, so do not assume it is always harmless. Attacking one can anger nearby zombified piglins. It does not barter like an ordinary piglin.

fire.answer: It is immune to ordinary fire and lava damage. That does not protect it from every other kind of damage.

sunlight.answer: Ordinary sunlight does not make it take burning damage. It is fire-immune, although other environmental hazards can still matter.

water.answer: It can breathe underwater.

health.answer: Bedrock zombie villagers have 20 health points (10 hearts).

spawning.answer: Zombie villagers can spawn with zombies, generate in abandoned villages and igloo basements, or result from villagers being killed by zombies. Infection depends on difficulty.

drops.answer: Zombie villagers can drop rotten flesh, rare iron ingots, carrots or potatoes, and applicable equipment under their own loot conditions.

interactions.answer: Apply Weakness, then feed a normal golden apple to start curing a zombie villager. Protect it while it converts. An enchanted golden apple is not the curing ingredient.

taming.answer: Zombie villager cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: You cannot breed a zombie villager.

curing.answer: Apply Weakness, then use an ordinary golden apple directly on the zombie villager, not an enchanted golden apple. Keep it protected while curing; it can still attack. Curing usually takes three to five minutes. A baby stays a baby, and a previously traded villager keeps its profession and trades.

conversion.answer: Zombie villagers can be cured using Weakness and a normal golden apple. This process does not cure ordinary zombies, husks, drowned or zombified piglins.

fire.answer: Without protection, ordinary fire and lava can damage it. Being undead, large, or adapted to a particular biome does not by itself grant fire immunity.

growth.answer: Baby undead of this kind do not normally grow into adults while they remain undead. A cured baby zombie villager can later grow as a living villager.

variants.answer: Zombie villagers can have different biome outfits and profession appearances and can be babies or adults. Curing returns them to villagers.

spawn_conditions.answer: Zombie villagers can occur during ordinary zombie spawning, in abandoned villages and igloo basements, or when villagers are killed by eligible zombies. Infection chance is 0% on Easy, 50% on Normal and 100% on Hard. A bed alone does not generate one.

experience.answer: The base reward is 5 experience points for an adult or 12 for a baby after an eligible player or tamed-wolf kill. Naturally spawned equipment can add experience; items picked up later are a separate category.

experience_baby.answer: The base baby reward is 12 experience points after a player or tamed-wolf kill. Naturally spawned equipment can add more; this is different from ordinary baby animals giving no experience.

attack_style.answer: Zombie villagers use zombie-style melee attacks. They are still hostile while waiting to be cured, and babies can move quickly.

provocation.answer: A zombie villager is hostile rather than a normal trading villager. It does not need to be attacked before it targets players.

counterplay.answer: Contain it safely if you want to cure it, and protect it from sunlight. Apply Weakness and then use a normal golden apple; do not release it among villagers before curing finishes.

lifetime.answer: In Bedrock, zombie villagers created by converting villagers are persistent. Abandoned-village and igloo-basement examples are also persistent. Ordinary naturally spawned zombie villagers can need a name tag to prevent normal despawning. Peaceful can still remove them.

relocation.answer: A minecart can carry a zombie villager in Bedrock. Bring an empty cart into contact with it, then use rails and powered rails along a protected route. An active activator rail can eject the passenger. It can still be dangerous while riding; a cart is not taming or protection from its attacks. The cart alone does not guarantee persistence in Bedrock.

combat.answer: It is a hostile mob and can attack players. Apply the appropriate Weakness effect and use a golden apple to begin curing it under suitable conditions.

sunlight.answer: It can burn in direct sunlight when unprotected. Shade, water and applicable armor protection can prevent that; sunlight protection does not make it immune to lava.

water.answer: It can breathe underwater.

spawning.answer: Place a painting item against a suitable supporting wall. Paintings are decorations, not naturally spawning animals.

drops.answer: A broken painting can return its painting item. Removing its support makes it pop off; it is not a source of animal loot.

interactions.answer: Leave enough clear space for the painting size you want. Painting support and placement rules differ from placing a solid building block.

identity.answer: A painting is a decorative entity hung on a wall. Its size and picture depend on the available space and placement choice.

behavior.answer: A painting is a decorative entity hung on a wall. Its size and picture depend on the available space and placement choice.

reference.name: Painting
reference.what: A painting is a decorative entity hung on a wall.
reference.does: Its size and picture depend on the available space and placement choice.

spawning.answer: Dropped items appear when players drop inventory items, blocks break, containers spill or creatures produce loot.

interactions.answer: Most dropped items despawn after five minutes while their area is ticking. Time pauses while the area is unloaded. Bedrock nether stars do not normally despawn.

drops.answer: A dropped item already represents its item stack. Pick it up rather than trying to kill it for another loot drop.

identity.answer: A dropped item is the world entity representing an item outside an inventory. Players can pick it up, and compatible nearby item stacks can merge.

behavior.answer: A dropped item is the world entity representing an item outside an inventory. Players can pick it up, and compatible nearby item stacks can merge.

reference.name: Dropped Item
reference.what: A dropped item is the world entity representing an item outside an inventory.
reference.does: Players can pick it up, and compatible nearby item stacks can merge.

spawning.answer: Gravity-affected blocks such as sand and gravel become falling-block entities when their support is removed.

drops.answer: The result depends on the falling block and its landing space. It may settle, break into an item, or be destroyed; not every falling block guarantees an item.

interactions.answer: Falling anvils and pointed dripstone can hurt entities below. Suspicious sand or gravel loses its archaeological contents when it falls and breaks, so support it before excavating.

identity.answer: A falling block is the moving entity form of a gravity-affected block. It can settle into a block when it lands, or break under unsuitable conditions.

behavior.answer: A falling block is the moving entity form of a gravity-affected block. It can settle into a block when it lands, or break under unsuitable conditions.
